Skirt steak, NY strip, hake and ravioli - all winners. Great advice about ordering medium rare; it did arrive medium. Seated by the open kitchen we actually enjoyed all the great fragrances. Service was knowledgeable but overwhelmed by full house. Pass on the house salad - too plain. Desserts were excellent. Rich flourless chocolate cake, exceptional flan but best were wispy lemon cookies. Friendly crowd - but those who dined late had fewer choices and did not get the duck fat fingerlings. Really felt sorry for them. Groupon got us in the door but all agreed menu offered value and savor. Bring a bottle or two, arrive by 7ish and enjoy!

text: This was my first trip to the Webster Groves Big Lots. Will it be my last? Well who knows. I live in South City so I normally shop at the South Kingshighway location. Now let me say Big Lots in general seem to just have awful customer service. The location on Kingshighway is not to much better than the one here at Webster Groves. I understand why Big Lots has terrible customer service.... They have low prices, and low overhead which includes minimal labor, so good luck finding help on the sales floor. They just are not staffed for customer service. Not that the employees are necessarily rude in general, its just they are pretty much always understaffed. So to an extent you need to expect this anytime you go to Big Lots and for the most part this is not a real problem unless you want furniture. Big Lots has a fairly large furniture department, and I wonder how much furniture they can sell, because it is very hard to find any help in the furniture department. I managed to purchase a sofa from the south city location, and this was an act of patience and determination. I had to wait for a sales associate and make it very obvious I needed help. The reason I drove to the Webster Groves location is because I attempted to purchase a computer desk from the south city location and they were out so I decided to check out the Webster Groves store. So I go out there and I walk around the furniture department and low and behold there is my desk! And what do we have here? A sign that says it is on sale for $49.99! Fortune smiles upon me! The sign says to see a sales associate on the desk. So I wait around the furniture department for like 20 minutes. I get tired of waiting and they have the furniture kits underneath the floor models. So I go and attempt to find a flat cart. I can't find one nor can I find any sales personnel to ask. So I decide to put it in a regular cart and head for the register. It took some work but I was on my way to having a new desk. I go to the register and the desk rings up $69.99. I tell the lady checking me out that this desk is supposed to be on sale for $49.99. She says "No....It is $69.99. I again reiterate that there is a display sign that this desk is on sale for $49.99. She looks puzzled and has a conference with another checker. They begin to dig around an add. I then tell them again about the display sign. The checker then decides to go get the sign, but her coworker thinks it would be better if me, the customer goes and retrieves it. Fine, whatever... I will go get it. So I go and get the sign and begin to make my way towards the registers, and the checker meets me halfway. I hand her the sign and she looks at it for almost a minute, and comes to the conclusion that it is real. Oh and this whole time a third Big Lots employee this older lady is just standing behind the cash register staring me down like she wants to kill me. The checker reluctantly sales the desk to me for $49.99. But she still has this uncertain look on her face like "Oh my gosh, did I do the right thing?" This was one of the most bizarre shopping experiences I have ever had. I think they thought I created a sign my self or something. I guess somehow they thought I had Big Lots signs that I brought in to get a desk 20 dollars cheaper. The third lady staring me down was the icing on the cake. The lack of knowledge of their products and even not knowing what their sales signs are about was a bit much to take in. They seriously were acting like I was doing something wrong. Other people would have left in disgust and frustration due to this horrible display of customer service, but not me. I wanted that desk for $49.99 and I got it! But it took patience.
label: NEG

text: OMG!!! Thank You God for Kien Giang in Nashville!!! We just moved from Chicago and after trying a few high ranking restaurants from Yelp we were getting really nervous. Nashville, you can thank Kien Giang for saving your hide! Weve eaten here 4 times so far and we havent even lived here 2 months. Ok, the food: Pho... its really the best weve ever had. We havent eaten pho in vietnam but weve had it at all the go to places in the major cities in the US and who would have thought that Nashville would house the holy grail of Pho? We always start with a pot of tea and an appetizer. Never had an appetizer we didnt like but their summer rolls will have you addicted. Perfect crunch, perfect flavor, perfect deliciousness. snAAAAck! Weve tried a lot of other things on their menu and its all good except their Banh Mi leaves a little to be desired. haha, and once you taste the pho you will totally forget about the way this place looks and the usual lack of service. They get your food to you in a timely fashion and will get you whatever else you need but they are not going to wait on you hand and foot. I mean come on guys, this isnt the capital grille. The last time we were there one of the waitresses was not happy with the cook and it gave the whole restaurant a good laugh. Everything is super cheap and I almost forgot: CASH ONLY If you forgot your Lincoln's there is an ATM close to the Kroger. (you will need to drive its not within walking distance) Oh, and when you are done just go up to the register and tell them your table number to settle your tab.

text: I frequent this spot every Friday for an afterwork nightcap. And despite the eccentric crowd, chaotic atmosphere, and PBR drinkers this place takes the cake for fun. Not trying to diss PBR drinking, but it many cases it will always lead to blackout drunkeness and debauchery, which is not my forte after a 10 hour shift. My first time here was on a whim with my gal pal and we danced the night away completely void of drink! We came back the following week for her birthday and were served stiff drinks and danced all night with the gogo ladies, who were very sweet an accommodating in making my girl's night special. We fell in love with the relaxed and super casual atmosphere, where no one was shy to dance and despite the fact we were in a room of strangers it felt like we knew everyone. The beer list is always favorable and whiskey is infinite. If you are going to eat, I would go for the Bison Burger, just delish, only complaint is they don't have fries! Its pretty busy on Fridays, but with the crowd in a constant state of drift, seats at the bar are always opening up. I have never been here before during daytime hours, but the nightlife is a must! If you're sick of overly priced dance clubs in center city, I highly suggest wandering off the beaten path (almost to the shadiest corner you can find) and enjoying a stiff drink and some good old dirty fun dancing and booze.

text: It is oh-so-ironic that I walked out of the establishment dissatisfied on the very day that I became the Duchess of Takenoya. I arrived on a busy Friday for lunch at 1:00 PM. My m.o. is always to grab a table, order the sashimi lunch special and a green tea matcha with boba, scarf it all down, and say "thanks and bye," within a space of 40 minutes. Today, I walked in, was ignored for about two minutes, and seated with a new menu, which much to my chagrin, no longer contained a list of lunch specials. I settled on a sashimi platter (twice the price of the old lunch special) anyway, and waited for someone to take my order. Five minutes passed, and I was still sitting there with my menu and not even a glass of water. I could tell this was not going to be a quick lunch, and looked around for my server. My neighbor's server. Anybody's server. No dice. I decided that since I had a 2:00 meeting, my best recourse was to get up and go. Honestly, the sashimi in my past experiences was really just OK, but was a good value for the price. Maybe I'll try again on a non-Friday, but if the lunch menu doesn't come back, Takenoya may just lose its only living Royalty.

text: When my friends suggested we go here for opening night, I was very excited. Twisted Tail sounded like a great little place for some well cooked pig and the whiskey/bourbon bar would be a bonus. I arrived a little after my party, was greeted and served a drink in a very timely manner and the cocktails were all mixed deliciously. I really enjoyed the Black Cherry Gimlet (...not trying to be miss know it all, but mixing a vodka/gin drink with lime juice does not a gimlet make) and the Time after Thyme. Service in this place is great. As far as the menu, to say I was disappointed to be at a place that clearly referenced swine in the name but has a total of three menu choices with pig (one has sausage, one has bacon, and the last seems like a pork shoulder) is an understatement. I also can't figure out what made anything on the menu consistent. Crawfish mac and cheese, duck spring rolls, flatbread and onion tarts... what? I got a salad and fries, because I'm on a diet... (not really.) and all of my friends ordered various appetizers. I know I should have ordered off of the entrees menu, but I wasn't really hungry and my friends and I tend to share anyway. The salad was good, but drenched in sweet dressing and the fries were good fries, but I feel like I paid $7 for a choice of three dipping sauces that were eh (chipotle ketchup, rosemary mayo, and agave nectar/vinegar). The crawfish mac and cheese was bland. The "spitfire chicken wings" were covered in a hoison glaze that tasted only of hoison glaze but had no semblance of cooked over an open fire (maybe it's a stretch to believe the wings were cooked over a fire, but it says SPITFIRE in the title). My friends liked their veggie options, but I didn't have any interest in trying any more food after the piece of crawfish I had was tough. After dinner, I tried to order some rye, but they were out of everything. The waiter explained "We just opened and some of these have been hard to find." And that was the final deal breaker for me. I get it, you just opened and the PA liquor board is full of Quakers or whatever, but print up new menus without teasing me. Will I come back? For the drinks, probably. The food, maybe if they pick up some herbs and spices and find some flavor.
label: NEG

text: If you are in need of a quick place to crash for the night, this place may or may not have a room. I wouldn't plan a vacation at this place or a stay longer than one night. The front desk lost my reservation and I was only able to get a room due to the fact that someone booked two rooms by accident. The room wasn't completely cleaned and looked like they quick wiped everything down and folded towels. There was dirt on the toilet and a panel in the wall was hanging down. Was scared to really look deeper into the room in case I found more filth. In the morning, upon us going down to breakfast, which was the ONLY positive thing in the stay, the cleaning ladies were very pushy. We walked out of the room, no intentions of checking out until we were done eating, and they kept asking when we were checking out and what room number we were in. This happened three times. When we went down to breakfast, coming back from breakfast, then again when we were leaving. I booked my room two months in advanced and yet somehow they lost my reservation. That took 2.5stars away right there, then with pushy cleaning ladies, dirty room, and a sketchy elevator that brought my review down to a 1. I would give another star for the breakfast being so good, but when the lost my reservation, it ruined the whole experience. They're lucky I didn't flip out.

text: Suppose you were a space alien and had just heard of Mexican food, perhaps seen photos or read a description on Wikipedia. Excitedly, you input all this data into the emulator and poof, out comes a fine looking Mexican dinner. This is about how Red Habanero seemed to me yesterday. The colors are right--the sauces are red and green. Even quality ingredients seem to be used. The problem is that the food just doesn't taste anything like Mexican food. Case in point: enchiladas made with flour tortillas and without any enchilada sauce or spices, just some red sauce thrown over the top. The guacamole was nice and green, but was just creamed avocado with no flavor or punch. Back in the day, when there was only El Sol and Chi-Chi's in Indy, Red Habanero might have been welcome. Now, with a plethora of authentic and semi-authentic Mexican restaurants all over town, I can't see any reason to go here. Chipotle is very close by and you'll get better food for less $.

text: Mmmmmm... spicy scallop hand rolls. NOM NOM NOM I just finished a nice round of take out from Sushi O Sushi. This being the first night of Snowpocalypse 2011, I decided to brave the empty streets of Nashvegas and slide on down to the local sushi spot. I figured they didn't carry any gallons of milk or loaves of bread, so I should be safe from the crazy hoarders. Surprisingly, there were about 5 tables occupied. I've eaten here about 7 or 8 times and have never had a bad meal. I like places that get original with rolls and mix it up a little. They do some amazing things with fresh fruit and fish here. The Double Double roll is AMAZING. The Spicy Tempura roll was excellent. Their prices are on the slightly above average side for Nashville, but their variety, quality and freshness make up for it. Their specialized rolls take up about 3 pages in the back of the menu and each has a decent picture/description to accompany it. With this, you get a good idea of how it is prepared, which always helps when trying something new. Unfortunately, this also gives you soo much to choose from which can be tough to narrow down. On a side note, I did get annoyed at the Droid Yelp app because it told me I was too far to check in, although I was sitting at the sushi bar. Overall, this is a good sushi spot in South Nashville. Yes, the sushi menu is big, but their food is good enough to keep coming back to try all of the rolls.

text: The two star description of Teavana is dead on - 'meh, I've experienced better' is so Teavana. Don't get me wrong, for those hard pressed to find good tea options in NashVegas, you need a Teavana and its location in Green Hills is both a blessing and a curse. The upside is that you can access it from many neighborhoods without too much of a haul, and the downside is it's Green Hills Mall with it's ridiculously small parking spaces grabbed up by an abundance of what would seem to be drunk SUV drivers. The tea is great and the service is pretty good. The whole family loves the samples and machines and I've been introduced to some great teas at this place. The downside, and this is coming from an upper middle class person, is the price. Its simply so far over the top as to border on the ridiculous. As much as folks laugh at Starbucks for a $5 frappacino, you will drop that on a much smaller drink here with 2/3s of you cup filled with ice. There are no bargains here. Even the smallest bag of tea will cost you $15 and the staff will wistfully over scoop and then stare blankly when you balk at $75 for two tiny bags of tea. My lesson is to stop by, browse, taste the samples and buy from a good on line vendor which charges 20% of what they are scalping you for at Teavana.
label: NEG

text: I love working out at the Y! This location has a good variety of class offerings including spinning, body pump, yoga and Zumba. The outdoor pool is small but is usually sufficient for the number of swimmers. I advise most people to check the swim schedule each day so they can avoid going when the high school swim teams are practicing, otherwise the pool is too crowded. The pool is heated in the winter so it is still possible to get a nice swim - just walk quickly after you get out! The staff here all seem very friendly and helpful and there's a wide range of personalities among the trainers so it should be no problem to find someone that you click with. One limitation to this location is that it shares part of the facility with a church. Because of this the facility does not open until the afternoon on Sunday and the gymnasium is often closed for other services and activities. The Y usually offers a free three day pass so it's easy to come try everything out and see if it works for you.

text: ...ALERT...Since this review, El Meson is under new ownership and it appears they are correcting the decor, food, and service. I will take a moment to review this location again in the future. I love Mexican food and I am not sure this qualifies as either Mexican nor food. The plus side is the place has a very festive, colorful, and modern decor. There is usually plenty of wait staff to serve/take orders and the owner is a really nice and pleasant guy. They are heavy handed on the top-shelf margaritas too. The price is right for the majority of the menu items. The down side is there is not enough space to type it all here, so I will recap. The menu selection is too large. By that I mean, I always question any restaurant can produce great quality food with a menu that covers over 75+ dishes. How can they keep all those ingredients fresh to scale their menu options? The food is bland and reminds me of school lunches on Mexican day. The rice/arros is lifeless, bloated, and amateurish. The beans/frijoles are grayish, brown wall spackling at best. The chips taste like they were made quite a bit ahead of time along with the salsa and guacamole. The main dishes lack any creativity, flair, distinction, or the slightest element that suggests they were not taken from a frozen section of the grocery store and microwaved on site. Come on amigos...its' MEXICAN FOOD and it is your hallmark to prepare and serve this food with some respect. Make the tortilla chips, salsa, and guacamole fresh at least. After all, they are low food cost and simple to prepare. Mexican food can be beautiful, flavorful, and memorable. It is supposed to be zesty, spicy, and FRESH. I would not recommend this place even on a budget.

text: Howl at the Moon is almost always a must see destination when I see it in a city, and so when I saw it here in New Orleans, I wandered in. The nice thing is the fact that there is no cover at this location, and during happy hour they have 3 for 1 specials. They also serve the delicious Abita beer there. Unfortunately this place pales when compared with the KC location. (I never thought that I would say that a location in middle America provided better entertainment than a similar location in a tourist hot spot like New Orleans). The help was attentive once they realized we were there (which took up to 15 minutes). But getting noticed amongst the few tables they had there was difficult. The musicians there were decent, but again the KC location beats them hands down. Firstly, even on a weekend night they had a partial band. In KC I saw a violinist, a guitarist, bassist, keytarist and a drummer all playing in the background at a given point during the night. Secondly, the musicians play what they want to play, and if they don't like what they are paid to play they will give a dollar amount to overcome that. To me that is simply poor performanceship. Lastly, when the crowd isn't participating they rely on this annoying block sounding machine to give the crowd a rhythmn to clap to. It sounds like a metronome that drowns out the piano depending on how close to the stage you are. In KC usually the crowds don't need to be prompted to clap along. A howl fan I am, but this location fails when it comes to providing the experience. Instead, when you go to the bathroom and hear good music playing, wash your hands, then follow the sound to the Saloon next door. It is worth the trip and if the braille blues band is playing, kick back, grab a drink and relax! (the bathrooms serve 3 different locations.

text: I waited for a special moment to write about Betty's Speakeasy. Maybe now that my belly is full of delicious lunch from there, I am ready. I have had the sauteed greens sandwich, served on their delicious homemade beer bread, and just recently the roasted zucchini/eggplant (mine came with eggplant because they were out of zucchini), served with a tasty little side salad and PICKLED corn on the cob. I didn't even know you could do that. WOW. The thing that so clearly shouts LOVE from this place is the fact they use only fresh local produce, so they pretty much cook with whatever is on hand. If they run out they'll try to substitute something (ie the roasted eggplant, win), and everything is house made fresh and delicious. The breads, pastries and sweets are all to die for. Cupcakes & fudge are both unique and special. The beer bread is bananas. Not as in made with bananas, as in ridiculously good I don't have a word for it. text: What is wrong with you people? Last night was the Chinese New Year, so we finally bit the bullet and actually had a sit down meal here, after having their take-out at least twenty times. First was a pot of their house special soup, a mix of wontons, meat and vegetables in the most delicious broth I've had in a while. The wontons were exceptionally juicy and just the right consistency to grab with chopsticks without the things totally falling apart. Even the pork pieces were prepared to somehow absorb a ridiculous amount of broth, so chewing on a piece felt like I was also chewing on broth. Amazing. One entree was spicy black pepper beef, which maybe could have had more beef, but also I'm glad David's cares that I get my serving of vegetables. The other was salt and pepper squid. Having eaten at so many mediocre restaurants lately, I can barely remember how to describe the sheer pleasure of enjoying something so simple and so novel (to me) and delicious. The boyfriend described it well when he said the coating tasted like a Lay's potato chip. I was in love with the chewy texture inside and crispy coating outside. I may never eat fried chicken again. The total bill was puny, like, $40 with tip, and we still had leftovers to take home with us. To recap: Excellent food, lightning service, courteous staff, reasonable prices, and open till 3 in the freaking morning (4 on weekends). Oh and they have a ginormous 3D dragon on one wall. text: Sorry Nosh, but there really isn't much positive we can say after our experience there today. We picked this place for breakfast on an early Sunday morning, because most other places in the area didn't open until 8:00, and we had to get to the airport. Long story short, we arrived at 7:45am, got our food at 8:37am. We should have just gone to one of the good restaurants that opened at 8:00. Nosh is a little greasy spoon type diner with about 9 tables, and a wooden half wall between the cooking area and the dining area. When we arrived, there was one guy waiting on about 3 tables, and he was already flustered. It took about 5 minutes for him to ask us if we wanted anything to drink, another 5 minutes to bring our iced tea. At 8:30, 35 minutes into the fiasco....we started asking about our food......'it's coming right up'. Another 10 minutes....'we're just waiting on the tator tots". Another 10 minutes and the tator tots arrived, followed by the food a few minutes later. As far as the service, we didn't once get a refill on the iced tea. The 'sliders' came without the cheese. The eggs were cold. The 'hash brown' were diced red potatoes with onions......that's not HASH BROWNS. Bottom line, it's Mardi Gras.....you're going to get busy. Have more than one person working, and don't try to get out a bunch of 'take out' orders when customers are sitting waiting for their food. When someone asks for their food 25 minutes after ordering, it shouldn't take another 15 minutes to deliver........and then the order was incorrect and BAD. I DO NOT RECOMMEND.

text: Interestingly enough, I received a message yesterday from the VP of Sales at the Chester Springs location requesting that I remove my Yelp review of the dealership because "a lot has changed" since I posted my comment, and because my comment is 2 years old. First of all, whether the incident(s) I described occurred yesterday or 2 years ago it doesn't change the fact that this was MY personal experience. I didn't realize there was an expiration date on my opinion. \sarcasm Secondly, my issues with the car were not limited to what I experienced and wrote about here on Yelp (so my bad for not following up) 2 years ago. I had problems sporadically up until the year my lease was up and I returned the vehicle. Since the engine was repaired for the valve spring (Summer 2009), the power-steering died on me (Fall 2009) while I was sitting on the Broad St exit of 95N heading to a Phillies game (mind you, I never attended the game because once I made it into the parking lot I had to call Roadside Assistance and wait for a tow), and finally the catalytic converter failed (Summer 2010) and needed repairs/replacement (I honestly can't remember if it just required a repair or if they replaced the part altogether - whatever, just add it to the list). In defense of the Service Dept, the service manager and I became rather close (super-nice guy and really went above and beyond the call of duty for me - replaced 2 tires, free of charge as an expression of goodwill). He made sure I always had a loaner vehicle at my disposal for as long as I needed. Granted this is something Lexus advertises as one of their many service perks, but many times I was showing up at the dealership on the spur of the moment and there isn't always a guarantee that a loaner car will be available on an impromptu basis. In fact, the time I took the car in for the catalytic converter all of the loaner vehicles were in use, so the service manager lent me his personal vehicle for the weekend. So my response to the request to remove my review? Sorry, but I stand by my review and will not take it down from Yelp. This is my personal experience and my opinion of the product. I gave kudos where they were due (and I believe my 2-star rating reflects that), however the positives and the passage of time do not negate the series of events. It is those events that led me to the decision to NOT go with Lexus for my next vehicle. Some people may swear by the brand and have experienced nothing but rainbows and unicorns with their vehicle; good for them - I wish them all the luck in the world. As far as my new car is concerned, I'm cautiously optimistic.

text: My Actual rating is 0.5 star, only if i can.....I give the 0.5 because it's BYOB and the location (Olde City)...but i was told by management BYOB is going away soon because they got a liquor license now. As for the food, I'm not sure if it's because of all the liquor that other people are drinking before they come here to eat or the ones they drink during the meal...but i really can't see how Han Dynasty is rated that high. This is the second meal that I wish i can ask for my money back! I was here for a birthday party so I can't send my food back in; we're a group of 15+. We ordered quite extensively and I haven't started drinking yet. So my review isn't skewed by alcohol. We ordered and I tasted all: Appetizer * Chicken in Chili Oil * Pork Belly in Garlic Sauce * Beef & Tripe in Chili Oil * Beef Tendons in Chili Oil Entree * String Beans w/ Minced Pork * Eggplant w/ Garlic Sauce * Fish Dry Pot Style * Three Cup Chicken * Fish Black Bean Style * Chicken Garlic Sauce Style Everything we order is poorly executed, even down to the simple task of cook steam rice! This place is a joke, how can you not know how to cook rice and call yourself Chinese (Szechuan) restaurant. It's just putting it the rice cooker with the proper level of water and "push" the cook button. Han Dynasty rice is hard and dry, the rice kernel haven't even popped yet and they are serving it to their customers. There's only two reasons for this rice debacle (improper rice to water ratio during the cooking process or just plain undercooked). I love Szechuan food and I eat it quite often, so I had the good and the bad. Han Dynasty was in a league of its own. It's just a small step above inedible. I don't understand how all the appetizers we had can be so salty and taste the exactly the same, just plain hot! It's like they just threw a fistful of salt, and then lather it with chili oil. Szechuan cuisines are known for having slow simmering spice, each spice touching different taste buds creating this complex level of spicy and distinct flavor. Hans Dynasty, their so called "Szechuan" food either tasted, salty, spicy (as in all hot and no spice), bland, undercooked or overcooked. Eggplant w/ Garlic Sauce was very salty with a hit of sourness. The Fish Dry Pot Style was overcooked, and bland. Three Cup Chicken VERY SALTY! I used the hot tea and washed the sauce away from the chicken, thinking I can savage it. It was STILL VERY SALTY after 3 wash, so I just gave up. Fish Black Bean Style was very dry...either they used frozen fish and fried it or they just overcooked it. I didn't care of the sauce it came with. It tasted like it came from the Lee Kum Kee can. Chicken Garlic Sauce Style, I had better in Chinese take-outs, it tasted the same as the Eggplant sauce, very salty with a hit of sourness. The String Bean was the only tolerable dish, still poorly executed but tolerable. It was bland and undercooked, which was very welcoming after all the salt and hotness that we had to eat. If I wasn't there for a birthday party, I would have send the food back, or just walk out. I really want to like and really was looking forward to eating at Han Dynasty with all the publicity it received "Travel Channel/ Yelp reviews". I even got lips from people for not having eaten there yet, and I call myself a foodie. Now that I did, I feel so jibbed. I regret spending one of my meals eating Han Dynasty food. These are calories which I feel sour having to work off because it's so not worth it!

text: I tore up some Bottom of the Sea on a Sunday night. My expectations for this place were pretty low after walking in--unimpressive and basic decor, somewhat dirty bathroom, and understocked bar. But then....it was like our waiter was sent from heaven as he slid a HUGE plate of crab legs smothered in garlic, spices, and butter in front of me. As I cracked and plucked the succulent crab from its shell I felt like a kid on Christmas day opening presents to find all the goodies inside. The corn and brocoli were good too, but the crab was definitely the star! ATTENTION ALL OTHER SEAFOOD RESTAURANTS: season your seafood even if it has a shell---it makes a difference! And I'm not just talking about sprinkling some Old Bay on top. My friend ordered the fried shrimp and crab cakes which were equally as good as the crab legs. In fact, it was the best fried shrimp I've ever had. We did not talk much during our meal....we both had a mutual understanding that this food was too good to waste it on some chatter. The $4 martini special was nice, however the martini glasses were small and the drinks were on the weaker side. Opted for beer for the next round....can never mess up beer or wine. Our waiter was very friendly and attentive. However, I think he could tell that he did not need to check in on us often because he probably heard all the "Mmmmmms" and "Ooooooos" and "OMG this is so good" coming from our table. I have not been so satisfied with a seafood meal in a long time. At the end of my meal I was saying "Red Lobster Who?" since this restaurant put the Chain King of seafood to shame. You're not going to find foofy-foofy seafood here, but you will find FLAVORFUL seafood and HUGE portions. If this place remodeled and paid a more attention to cleanliness it would be phenomenal, but then again maybe I should overlook this so I can always get a table quickly.

text: This Company is actually a store. It sells chocolate. It sells coffee. It sells tchotchkes, usually containing coffee/chocolate. It has good lighting and paint that is the hue of fresh pollen. Its view of the Soldiers and Sailors Monument lets you see lots of funny people at all hours. Yesireebob, there's not much more to say that won't devolve this review into a personal anecdote, but the repeated personal experiences over a short amount of time have turned me away from a place I'd otherwise like to support. First off, the coffee/chocolate is of a quality that in accordance with the price. The price is fairly low. Need I complete the transitive equation? One other Yelper here blamed the problem on the fact that the chocolate was made way up in South Bend and then shipped...but c'mon folks: virtually NONE of the chocolate we buy was manufactured on site! Do you really go to Belgium every time you want Godiva? And aren't the Belgian choccies generally wonderful no matter where you purchase them, despite the fact that Indianapolis is not Brussels? Even if these get shipped freeze dried every day--or maybe BECAUSE they get shipped freeze dried--this chocolate is simply adequate. I confess: I'm no chocolate connoisseur, but I can certainly identify remarkable chocolate when I see it. This is not. Ditto for the coffee. Haven't tried the ice cream, but most Yelpers don't seem to rave. And that's a bad sign, because ice cream is like pizza: even when it's bad, it's still pretty good. Secondly, the "baristas" are a real mixed bag. They aren't terrible, but they don't personalize it a great deal. The place typically has functional wireless, and when it works most of the time it's great--when it doesn't work, staff seems indifferent to the idea of fixing it. But more irritating to me is their loose attitude toward smoking...yep, a coffee shop that turns a blind eye to it. Is this an Ethan Hawke-from-Reality Bites-hangout? Granted, I haven't seen it happen in the store itself, but on multiple occasions, people have smoked out on the patio--inches away from the no smoking signs (violating a company rule) and less than 8 feet from the entrance (violating a city ordinance). When I said I'd like to enjoy a seat outside but in the smoke-free environment that is promised by their rules, the manager of South Bend Chocolate Company crankily went out and moved the smoker out of the patio. But within 30 minutes, other smokers had followed suit, suggesting that manager only enforces the rule when someone asks for it. And on another day, Mr. Smoker from day one came to smoke again (right next to the entrance and next to no-smoking sign) and Ms. Manager came out and chatted him up. No enforcement. So I guess the rules don't apply if you are friends with management...? Typical. But not a place I'll patronize. And lastly, the restrooms in the basement are, another Yelper recognized, not for the faint of heart. Aside from being another place where smoking is obviously welcomed, they remind me of the basement of the Bishkek International Airport in Kyrgyzstan. (Actually, the smoking part makes it that much MORE like the Bishkek Airport.) Need I say more?

I've had flavorful beef before, this wasn't it. And oddly, despite all of the fancy supposedly spicy toppings it had... none of them helped. I would have been happy with the prices if food actually was flavorful and worth the effort they clearly put into the actual recipes (many of which sounded very interesting)... text: This is probably the finest remaining example of a traditional New Orleans neighborhood casual creole-Italian restaurant and one of my favorite places to eat. They basically have the vast majority of all the dishes that I LOVE in the New Orleans food repertoire. There is a fantastic selection of different daily specials every day they are open. Mandina's serves fantastic turtle soup, gumbo, po boys, seafood, etouffee, red beans and rice along with Irish influenced dishes like corned beef with cabbage and beef stew. Some people whine about their "Americanized" Italian dishes but I love them and I will drink their sweet awesome marinara sauce. The menu is a fantastic example of the glorious blend of all the ethnic backgrounds that melded to create our rich creole New Orleans food tradition. The quality of the food here had slipped a bit before Katrina and then it slipped a lot after and they were running on only 2 or 3 cylinders for awhile. Well now they are roaring along on all 8 cylinders, like a fine tuned race car, and the food is once again fantastic! They have also FINALLY started taking credit cards!!! They only thing that remains to be a great inconvenience here is the sheer popularity of the place, as there is often a long line to get inside, but that is just further proof of how great this place is. The one thing that would make this place even more fantastic would be the addition of an oyster bar as the lack of raw oysters is a significantly felt and glaring omission in a place such as this. For the portion sizes you get here it is extremely hard to beat the fantastic value that this place offers. If you want to experience the epitome of traditional "everyday" New Orleans food this is probably the single best place to look into its soul. Mandina's is what a lot of places in New Orleans used to be and it's the "it" that many places are still trying to recapture. Sure there are all sorts of new places and innovative "new" spins on food but when it comes to my dining raison d'être of NOLA food my orbit will always be drawn to circle the bright sun of the traditional dishes here. Tip: I'm not a fan of the turkey and oyster dressing plate here as it just doesn't taste good to me and I much prefer the Thursday turkey special at Joey K's and I have to say the same for the corned beef.. Once Again: They NOW Finally Take Credit Cards!!! Hooray!!!

text: My wife and I started going to this place after we became sick of Las Palmas on 8th by Kroger. Maybe it's only a by comparison thing, but we've been really happy here. Is it authentic or real special? No, but after Las Palmas became more a la carte, more gristle in the chicken, and watered down tiny margaritas, this place seems like heaven. The deck is huge and a plus. You can even feed the finches and grow in cholesterol together. When no one is looking of course. And the wicker light fixtures kick ass. They get half a star solely on the fixtures and the struggling rose bush by the front door. I also like that half of the original flourescent cabana sign is now enclosed with the patio. They also have old tube TV's on the porch, usually not too loud, and an impressive mix of ecclectic chairs and other things hung up in the rafters. Character counts, maybe more when drinking, but it counts. The food seems better to us not only because of larger portions, but better combinations and specials. I get a Special Burrito, one chicken, one beef, a little lettuce, sour cream, and salsa on top. Pretty dang good in my opinion. Haven't hit gristle yet. I get the feeling they want us to like the food and are trying. That is an improvement. Have also tried other mainstays typical of mexican places and I like them all. After we have two margaritas a piece, we are effectively able to get our buzz on. I can't ask anymore in that department, but admittedly am not very discriminating. They are not complete margarita mix bombs, and taste semi-strong at first. If I pucker up and get a shiver with a little bite on the first sip, that's a good thing! My wife is a vegan and she tries all kinds of stuff. She's pretty happy with the place and we've been going every other week or so with no complaint. I also must warn you that there is a Futon store next door. Futons remind me of all kinds of weird times in my life, but I am able to work thru it, and really enjoy this place! The staff is usually very nice and prompt. The other patrons sometimes are a little sketchy, but I don't feel threatened, and have even communicated in a friendly manner with some of them. Springer-esque looking folks sometimes, but I bet they think I look like wierd, so all is fair. I would def check this place out, and keep your hopes realistic. Go to taco mammacita or whatever that place is if you want flashy.

text: While we planned on dining at Padmanadi for Sarah's Birthday, we couldn't, as Padmanadi is closed on Mondays. So, we were in the neighbourhood and decided to give Veggie Garden a try. Tucked on a sidestreet, Veggie Garden isn't in the most obvious location, but it's still fairly convenient to downtown. The restaurant has a fairly up-to-date, if plain design and the restaurant (and washrooms) are very clean. Yes, you could take your neat-freak Aunt here. The food is pretty standard Vietnamese com chay (vegetarian food), plus a number of chinese fake meat favourites. Sarah and I greatly enjoyed the (fake) lemon chicken. We also relished the opportunity to enjoy WonTon Soup. The thin vegetarian spring rolls were also the best we've had in Edmonton. We also ordered a (fake) seafood noodle dish. Sarah was expecting chow mein noodles, but the restaurant used very fresh tasting thicker noodles instead. Sarah didn't like the fake fish texture, but i liked it a bit more. And like the other authentic Vietnamese restaurants in town, Veggie Garden serves a number of delicious fruit smoothies and other sweet drinks, including fresh lemon soda and vietnamese coffee (with condensed milk). I don't think Veggie Garden will convert any carnivores to vegetarianism, but it's a great addition to Edmonton's vegetarian food scene. Service is very friendly and Ky, the owner, was very thankful we found her restaurant and that we were eating there. They are open every day of the week.

I think this place has good food but can't keep up with the rush of people that have seen it on Triple D. They are going through growing pains trying to adjust to the bigger crowd. When I left, all the tables were full (about half had food) and there were 18 people in line to order. My advice, either wait a month or so to try it out when all the fuss dies down or drive by and look to see how many people are there. text: My boyfriend and I went to Parkway Bakery at the recommendation of a Tulane University faculty member - we had to trust him, right? He told us that it was the best spot in town for po' boys. I worked in a New Orleans style restaurant during my undergrad years so I am no stranger to the po' boy. I never thought they were anything to write home about. They are a little boring and usually have crappy bread. Those are the pretenses I brought with me to Parkway Bakery. I was pleasantly surprised and now have a new light into the world of po' boys. We sat in the bar area and took plenty of time reading through the list of what seemed to be 100s of po' boy options while sipping a Dixie beer - thank goodness the bartender was patient with us. I finally decided on the shrimp po' boy and J got the roast beef one. We shared a side of cheese fries...as if we didn't already have plenty of food. My shrimp po' boy was overflowing with juicy fried shrimp topped with all the fixins on warm soft bread. Glad I gave the po' boy another chance! Parkway Bakery is in a sketch part of town but well worth the trip. You can enjoy your food at the bar, in their dining area, or on their outside patio.

text: The Grand Sierra hotel (don't kid yourself, this is not a "resort") feels like the kind of place that might go out of business while you're staying there. This past weekend my wife and I booked a two night stay at the Grand Sierra and after the first night we checked out and switched hotels, it's that bad. The lobby and casino are nice enough. After the burn-out stoner snowboarder parks your car and you get inside you might even be tricked into thinking this is a nice place. Not so. I read another review on line that described the hallways in this hotel as something out of the Shining, and that's a dead-on accurate description. Murky, dark, loooooong corridors with a bizarre mixture of pseudo-Native American/Southwest inspired designs and an off-putting green/burnt orange color scheme come together to make you certain that around the next corner (if you ever get there) you'll find a pile of hacked up children. If the goal is to get you to RUN to your room and RUN to the casino... goal achieved, I don't want to spend any more time in this creepy hallway than I have to. As for the rooms themselves... well... 1989 called and wants their TV's back. I haven't seen a TV this old outside of a pawn shop. Uncomfortable beds? Check. Cramped old fashioned bathroom with hideous wall paper? Check. Backwards rotating knobs in the shower so you get sprayed with freezing water? Check. Low shower nozzle that bashes you in the head while trying to shampoo? Check. Horrible view of a parking lot out the window? Check. Sign threatening to charge you for the bathrobe and coffee maker that *weren't even in the room in the first place*? Check. OK, well what about the other parts of the "resort". First let's brave the creepy Stephen King elevators that open their yawning mouths as if they'll swallow you up forever. Beneath the casino is the arcade level. Down in the bowels of the hotel the hallways are easily 20 feet wide, you could race Hummers side-by-side down here, and it's just as murky and creepy as the hallways to the rooms. Honestly it feels like something out of a post-apolcalyptic zombie flick, this is where people would hole up to try and survive while sending out the strongest to hunt for food and fire wood. The few "shops" downstairs all have the odor of imminent death as well, not a single soul inside doing any shopping. The actual arcade is nice, plenty of games and a big play area for the kids, plus one star. But the other businesses on this level feel like any minute you might see a crying owner shuttering the doors and then you'd hear a gunshot and a thud as their lifeless body crumples to the ground. Seriously. This place is awful. I've never been in a hotel before where I could almost literally hear the wind sighing the words "Geeeeeeeet oooouuuuuuttttttt". Let's check out the pool, it should be nice. Ooops, CLOSED. Let me wend my way past the area where pets are brought outside to poop and then, yep, past the smoking section.... wow this place really could use some landscaping... and paint.... and art.... and a wrecking ball..... Back upstairs, we checked out the bowling alley. Very nice! Well lit, lots of people, clean... it served as a stark counterpoint to the dank, weird chasm we had just emerged from downstairs. Anyways you get the point. This place bites. And if that's not all enough here's a couple of other jtems: - 20 minute wait on hold on the phone to get the front desk to initiate our early checkout, when I mentioned the hold time I was told "Yeah, that's cuz we're busy." - Pool = Closed. No indoor pool - Spa = No towel racks? No bench to set things one? Ok I'll just put my stuff... on the... floor? Thanks. We normally stay at the Atlantis, and thought we'd try something "different". Ooooops. We went to the Atlantis for the next night, it was great. Steer clear of the Grand Sierra unless you're one of the producers of Ghost Hunters or some other show that highlights old places full of spooky, lonely hallways and not much else of any interest. One star, plus one star for nice arcade, bowling alley and casino. Visit if you want, but DO NOT stay here.
label: NEG

I'm not even sure that he apologized. 3) The waitress was great. 4) They were out of at least 4 of the house beers. 5) The food was mediocre at best. I got the mojo pork dish and my husband got the meatloaf. The caesar salad was the best park of the meal, it was very good. The main dishes were bland and underwhelming. 6) They offer 4 or 5 types of bread pudding for dessert. They were out of 2 of them. 7) It smells bad. I'm not sure if it's a garbage/dumpster smell or a dirty mop water smell, but every few minutes I would get a whiff of a very unpleasant odor. Everyone in my party experienced the smell. text: My wife and I came here on New Years Eve and were subject to the special Holiday Menu. It all looked good and we went there based on a review in our hotel magazine. I also liked the fact that it was a local business wanting to use as many local products as possible. The setting being in an old house as well also helped make our deicison. We arrived and had to wait a few moments to be seated, this was expected being New Years Eve, so it was no big deal. There was a nice dark room to sit near the bar which was very relaxing. The staff asked us if we wanted to drinks and that we would be seated shortly. No problems here. When we were seated, we were enjoying a local musician at the piano singing everything from Billy Joel to Elton John to basically everything on the Classic Rock station. She was enjoyable for the evening and very welcoming to all the patrons and took requests. Our server surprised us from behind as our seats were put in a way to face the stage. He went over the menu with us and we ordered our appetizers and dinner. My wife started with a salad. It was decent but nothing over the top. I ordered the rabbit pate and found it pleasant. For dinner, my wife order the half chicken. It looked good, but it was rather tasteless. The barley on the side was tasteless as well. I ordered the advertised New York Strip medium rare, which turned out to be a rib eye instead according to our server. That sparked my interest even more since I like that cut better. The steak came out and was undercooked. The server even asked me to check while he brought it to the table. Hmmmm.... It was still rather rare and in about five minutes he brought it back and it was cooked to my liking. After a few bites, one would expect a little fat here and there, but when each piece turned out to be fatty and stringy, I was getting annoyed. On top of all this, the steak was way too thick to be the rib eye's that I am accustomed to. I am almost thinking it was a chuck steak bought in bulk for New Years made to look like something else. I sent back the steak and decided to order the pork chop instead. The pork chop probably faired much worse than it actually was as my appetite was waning. The side of mash potatoes was decent but by that time I was done. I felt that all the servers were running around frantically for no reason. My wife and I both have worked in the restaurant business so I want to make it clear that I am not just complaining. They were far from understaffed but could not seem to accomodate their tables in a timely manner. At many times, I found servers hiding in the bathroom hallway or servers not even present and rarely coming out of the kitchen area. I cannot speak for other tables, but for the few around us, there were not many smiles based on the service and the food. If something was happening in the kitchen, it was very obvious on the faces and personalities of the servers. At the end of the night, our server tried to make nice with us and tried to make conversation over my wife's South American name. It did not help his tip at all. I think he knew we were upset with his service as well as the food. All in all, the best part of the evening was actually the OK lounge act the restaurant offered. She made the rounds to each table and wished us all a Happy New Year. What bothered me even more was that the restaurant was not overcrowded. There were empty tables scattered throughout and still the servers were unable to perform their jobs properly. The kitchen had a smaller menu for the holiday and still they were not able to make quality food for the price we were paying. The restaurant must have known what the dinner service was going to be like with the reservation book as well as the usual walk-ins. This restaurant we will definetly overlook the next time we are in town to visit.
label: NEG

She seemed to put in a lot of effort, curling it with a straightener, hairspraying as she went, and attempted to give my crown some volume using some sort of white powder, and finishing with a whole lot of hairspray. Unfortunately, by the end of it, I had a big huge, frizzy helmet of hair. Not quite the loose curls we had discussed and she had shown me in a picture book at the start of the appointment. When I came home, my boyfriend couldn't help but laugh and asked me why I didn't just do it myself. With only half an hour to make it to the wedding, I tried to salvage the hairstyle as much as possible, which was difficult with so much product in it. Between the wedding and reception, I came home, washed it out and deep conditioned since my hair felt so dry and ratty - which I originally thought was due to all of the product in it. After blowdrying, I honestly couldn't believe it was my hair that I was looking at. I had random chunks of hair, mostly towards the front of my head, and ends, that were completely singed and damaged. I could hardly comb through it, and could do nothing to make it presentable. Frantically, I texted my stylist who was out of town on vacation, asking if it was even possible to burn my hair with a straightener. He said it was very rare, and she would have had to hold it on the hair for an extended period of time, or go over it too many times in a short period. Unfortunately, I had trusted she knew what she was doing and hadn't paid much attention. A few days later, I went to my stylist, and verified that yes, my hair had been severely damaged by the hair straightener. I was forced to cut 5-6 inches off the front of my hair, and about 2-3 inches off the entire length, with more needing to be cut in the future. Some of the pieces in the front are damaged almost to the root, and will need to be cut over a period of time. My normally straight, shiny hair, is now a damaged, dull and frizzy disaster. I was heartbroken. Knowing that my hair could not be fixed, I tried to contact Blo's owner, to try to determine what could have gone wrong and to prevent this from happening to another client. I tried multiple times to get ahold of her, and was eventually told she only worked Friday and Saturdays, so I left a message for her to call me back. She was very nice on the phone, thanking me for being so nice about everything, and told me the girl who did my hair is a licensed esthetician, but not a stylist. She said she wanted to find out what happened and would contact the product rep and get back to me the following Monday. I have been waiting for that call for over a month. Due to my horrible experience and lack of customer service provided by Blo, I would not only strongly urge girls considering booking an appointment to think twice, but also caution you to evaluate what your hair is worth. Saving the $20 from getting it done at a professional salon, was so incredibly not worth it. I had known hair could be damaged by bad dye jobs, but was shown at Blo, that it can also be destroyed simply by styling. Proceed with extreme caution. You can probably do a better job on your hair yourself. I know I could have.

I could have walked a block down the street and had a much more pleasant experience ordering a much better pizza and less watered-down Coke at the Santa Barbara Brewing Company for a dollar or two more, and it would have been far, far better. The lock on the (unisex) bathroom door was non-functional, but this was not apparent when I tried to lock it. text: Waxing woes... Let's start at the end. I walked home shaking and crying. But I look at it as my duty to protect prospective customers from horrific experiences like the one I recently endured. Stupidly, when making the appointment, I didn't ask for Nelly this visit. Let that be known from the get go as I've had Nelly done my wax jobs before and found her to be top notch. I've waited several days since the appointment to make sure I didn't write the under the influence of pain or anger. I won't name the technician in this review. I'm in this conundrum. I don't want to mess with this torturer's, I mean *woman*'s livelihood, but I also can't help but think she should find another career. Say, prison guard. At Rikers. I'm sorry, but I don't think those folks deserve that either. I can't tell if she's a true sadist, because despite some awkward conversation held for seconds while my most tender region was being ripped and pulled repeatedly, she was silent. Instead of keeping my mind off of the procedure at hand, all I could do was silently scream in my head, as I quivered and begged for the bullet. I would have rocked, too but that's hard to do in goddess pose. Now I ask you, wouldn't any seasoned professional technician NOT pour hot wax onto the same spots over and over again? But this woman did just that and kept doing that with no more than a "You need to get numbing cream from your doctor next time." Like there would be a next time. No GYN exam has been 1/10 as traumatic. I had to wonder... am I being punked? But, no. There were no cameras. Just the bitter glare of the high wattage light bulbs overhead burning into my retinas. Say something? I *yelled* something. Twice. And it wasn't "Kelly Clarkson!" Safe words don't exist in the waxing world, my friends. I would have made her stop but I knew I'd be paying greatly for this "service" whether I continued or not (Earthsavers, in their infinite wisdom, charges you for "missed" appointments and warn you repeatedly when making the appointment). So, after 15 minutes I turned off and went into survival mode where I was staring into space barely existing anymore. Seriously. In that moment I became one with Sybil. I composed songs. Sonnets. Yelp reviews. This horror show lasted a full 35 minutes. It never took that long before. So, Earthsavers, I bid you farewell. I loved Nelly but I will never step foot into your place again when I know that you keep on a woman who should not be allowed to bear a wax wand. No less in a posh spa where a Brazillian runs you 70 bucks before tip. That's the thing. And there's this thing where when you're done with getting a service at a so-called posh spa, where they ask you how was everything. That didn't happen and the girl who took my card barely noticed that I was clearly disturbed. Oh well, at least my house is spotless. Cleaning sprees. The cheapest therapy. text: Some thoughts: I initially found it very strange that so few of the Philadelphia- and New Jersey-area transit services I rode had Yelp listings. I guess I can understand each train line not having a listing yet, but Market East Station? So I spent a lot of time researching addresses, locations, and the like to make sure my First to Review reviews laid a good foundation for many useful, funny, cool reviews to come. And you know what happened? Within a day, the Yelp Philadelphia moderators (and whoever is in charge of Trenton) changed the titles of my listings. So my specific review of New Jersey Transit's Northeast Corridor Line magically turned into a review of "N J Transit"--and you know how much I hate needless spaces between initials--and my review of SEPTA's Trenton Line Regional Rail turned into a review of SEPTA. But that's stupid, because I had already reviewed SEPTA in a different review. So in the interest of making things simpler for its users, Philadelphia Yelp's moderators believe it's better to create duplicate listings. Really? Why would you go to the trouble of changing something as specific as a review of train line and not actually research whether what you're changing it to already exists? Actually, Philadelphia Yelp, I'd like to apply for a part-time job as a moderator. I'm really good at research and fact-checking, and I'm a public-transit geek. Back to Market East Station. It's subterranean. But unlike Radiohead's "Subterranean Homesick Alien," which is sad in a beautiful way, Market East Station is just sad. I didn't really feel homesick here, but I did feel like a kind of alien. Actually, I thought about Downtown L.A. in the mid-'80s and all that subterranean ridiculousness that was cool for all of three seconds and then became sad. And when I was doing research on Market East Station--because I really do research before I write reviews--I learned that the station opened in 1984, which partially explains why it reminded me of L.A.'s own crumbling underground attempts at revitalization. But I don't hate the place. It's actually a little comforting in an uncomfortable way, because discomfort can be familiar, and what we fear most is often the unknown, no matter how much better or easier or less stressful it can make our lives. What I'm really talking about are cellphones. And strange guys with neck tattoos who tell you, while you're waiting for your South Philly friend to call you back and/or pick you up, that Hurricane Irene is coming and that they've already evacuated Jersey. Even with my limited knowledge of local customs and jargon, I knew the guy was exaggerating. Evacuated Jersey? As in the entire state? I had just been there; and it didn't seem like 8,791,894 people were preparing for Armageddon. OK, maybe some of them were, but I didn't see them. So I gave Erin O./G. the agreed-upon fifteen minutes, waited another five, called her back, waited another five, and promptly found a taxi, which was very easy, by the way. The station seems really confusing. I didn't get confused, but I could see myself getting confused. It was very comforting waiting at the corner of 12th and Filbert, tattooed-neck guy's presence notwithstanding. (Actually, tattooed-neck guy was one of the least troubling of the people I ran into while waiting.) See, one of the people who laid out San Francisco's streets was from Philadelphia, so we have a Market Street, a Sansom Street (spelled differently), a Cherry Street, a Chestnut Street, and a Filbert Street! So while I waited near the corner of 12th and Filbert, I imagined myself on Filbert Street in San Francisco's Cow Hollow. That neighborhood is the furthest thing from scary, so it was fine. I'd like to visit this station many more times. And to partake of its subterranean-mall sadness. And to keep it going. Because the '80s were so hopeful for so many people even though they knew they were headed for the precipice. Kind of like 2007, actually.

text: I have to give it two stars. The location and restaurant are beautiful and the staff has been super friendly. I've been there twice this past week. The first time I had the cheese platter and their daily fish selection. They gave us warm bread for the cheese which was yummy. Everything was delicious. I left nothing on that plate. The salmon had crispy skin and was not dried out. It had a watercress salad, mixed mushrooms, haricots vert ( fancy for green beans), and beurre blanc. Perfection on a plate. My friend had the spring chicken which is two pieces of chicken breast served on top of a huge slice of heirloom tomato with some orzo pasta. It had a very nice herbed gravy to accompany it. I tried it and it was very tasty. Then I went back two days later..... I took my picky sister knowing that she would like the spring chicken. I told her she had to order it. I had the fish selection again which was scallops. I got the 1 oz of cheese to start with and it came with cold bread. It didn't taste the same. I got the corn chowder with dungress crab (9.00) which was very good. My sister had the small bibb salad which was not that good. It had nuts, a light vinegrette, and 2 slices of crispy prosciutto on top. But the salad was not good, very bland. My scallops were cooked nicely and were accompanied by fingerling potatoes and oyster mushrooms. There was also an whipped almond butter at the bottom of it all and it was disgusting. The texture was gritty and the flavor ruined the dish. It was hard to eat the scallop without getting some on it because it was spread all over my plate. My sisters spring chicken had no salt! The orzo pasta tasted like a diluted version of mac and cheese. The best thing on her plate was the heirloom tomato! Maynard's to me lacked consistency, maybe it was just my bad luck or my sisters bad karma but she said she would not go back. My first time there was wonderful but the second....uhmmmm not so much!

text: First thing, attire is definitely more on the dressy side. Try being the only loser in the restaurant wearing a hoodie, jeans, and flip flops. Not to mention the snide looks I got when I asked for a table. So men, do yourself a favor and dress yourself up a tad bit. Closed toed shoes and a collared shirt will suffice. The ambiance is significantly more grandeur than what i generally experienced in Miami. The view of the water was gorgeous in the evening sky lit by buildings on the other side. The service was impressive despite my fashion faux pas for inappropriate attire for the venue. Eric treated us well and gave some excellent suggestions to the menu. The most outstanding item of our meal: the Sangria de Cava. This white sangria made with champagne was the primary draw for bringing me here. Sure enough, it did not disappoint. The reason for return was the tapas. I didn't want to go overboard with tapas as to not overwhelm her experience with it. So we kept to two plates and shared an entree. The bread to start the meal was divine cuban bread (naturally). The Langostinos were pretty spectacular. The empanadas were good, though not what I think of when I think empanada. The top it with corn and black bean, but where's the grease on the empanada itself? It's a nice healthy twist if you're looking for that. We shared the arroz con pollo. The rice was drenched in a nice buttery sauce. It made the rice a little too mushy for my girlfriend. I wasn't too picky. We capped the evening with the crema catalana. Their take to creme brulee. It was nice. Though, I've had better. Next time, I think I'll want to stick with tapas. And perhaps a more traditional dessert? Flan, tres leches? Til we meet again, Columbia, know that I'll be thinking about you. As General MacArthur promised the Filipinos: "I shall return!"

text: This review is for the upstairs "fine dining" portion: I'd been wanting to try the rehash of Merchants after I heard the guys who own Patterson House and Paradise Park took it over. Those are two really good establishments (for what they mean to be...speakeasy or tourist dive) and I had reason to infer that Merchants would extend their record. And I was wrong. Started with a cocktail. Took a while (only because it was made downstairs at the bar) but was solid Patterson-house quality. My partner's extra dry martini had too much vermouth (more than none), but I understand only homeless people ask for a glass of gin and it's a strange request. Second was better. Got a couple of starters to split, even though there wasn't any inherently sharable on the menu. Got the beets and goat cheese (beets could have been a little more uniformly cooked, goat cheese was good but it wasn't dressed as the menu stated). Got the tomato starter too (good, but nothing to squawk at). We received a nice little amuse bouche, but it included goat cheese and tomato which we just ate 2 seconds before. Points for trying though! They were out of the fish stated on the menu (I don't remember what it was originally...red snapper?) but were substituting salmon in it's place. I still got it, but it had little flavor. Cooked nicely, but maybe the salmon overpowered what would have been a good balance. Not bad, just not good. The wilted scallions on it were tough and stringy and impossible to eat. My partner's dinner was worse...he got the pork and it was a really really nasty piece of meat. Fatty, but still dry, no flavor. Pork can be soooo good! We skipped dessert. Wasn't really worth the parking downtown. Overall the service wasn't BAD...it was just....strange. We had multiple servers throughout the evening, each was nice, but sort of unnerving to give one guy your drink order, someone else bring it out, yet another clean the table off...etc. The building itself is really cool looking, with history and the details to match. Downstairs looked a little better, and I may give it a whirl if I'm on lower broad for some reason. Eh.

text: An epic Saturday night disaster. Giving Talula's 2 stars instead of zero because after the fiasco, management did everything they could to make it up to us. Had a 9:15 reservation for 2 people -- our anniversary celebration. Were told they were running 15 minutes behind. No problem. At 9:45, after no communication, we inquired again. Then were advised we had 1 group in front of us. The hostess was neither apologetic nor kind about the situation. A manager intervened very shortly thereafter, apologized profusely and offered a free cheese plate. We were finally seated at 10 p.m., in the bar area. Not what we had in mind for our anniversary. If we had wanted to eat at a bar, we would have gone to Pub and Kitchen or GoodDog. Given the late hour, we took the table. Our knowledgeable waiter took drink orders, delivered beverages and then disappeared. We had to ask someone else to seek him out. There may have been confusion about our order because of the complimentary cheese plate on our table. We ordered at 10:40 p.m. The cheese plate selected by the manager was fantastic, special and arguably the best dish of the evening. We had the salad of raw tuna, which was fabulous, and the oxtail tortelloni. The broth for the tortelloni was overly salted, to the point of being nearly inedible. For main courses, we had the bluefish (very good) and the cod. The cod, like the tortelloni, was extremely salty. The main course arrived at 11:30. At that point, it was way too late to argue about it or substitute another dish. When our waiter inquired about the uneaten cod, we explained the issue. To the restaurant's credit, at the end of our meal, the manager came by and told us our dinner was on the house and would not let us pay for any of it. She encouraged us to come back another time and suggested trying on a less busy night. We genuinely appreciated that management took responsibility for what appears to be an unusual crater in Talula's food and service. With that said, it was a truly disappointing evening. I much prefer to write more positive reviews.

After a brief exchange in which I said that if the bear+balloons couldn't be delivered that day, don't worry about it, Chad Kremp contacted me and said that the order would be delivered that day. Sure enough, it was. Better yet, a second bear+balloons was delivered the next day! Obviously a clerical error, but better be thorough than not. All this was done from Europe via email. Exceptional service and product. Recommend Kremp!

text: This place is great for all sorts of occasions. My last visit was the result of another restaurant that I wanted to visit being close for the night. So to grab a late dinner, I went to Continental Midtown (mostly because I just paid for parking and didn't feel like moving the car again.) Service is excellent. The servers are extremely friendly and helpful when you ask for suggestions. The food itself was pretty good. My last meal here was the Korean Pork Tacos for the tapas course, then my friend and I got the Seared Tuna and the Jumbo Lump Crab Pad Thai. The Tuna was cooked perfectly on a bed of risotto which I personally felt took the spotlight of the dish. I felt that the Pad Thai begged for more of a jazzing up (if that even makes sense.) Instead of focusing on the core flavor and the texture of Pad Thai, I felt as if the dish was just thrown together quickly. My water was always full and the ambiance created a very chic and retro modern setting for a casual meal. Truly a "hip" restaurant more geared towards young professional (generation Y and above). This will definitely not be my last trip as it seems to always get better with each visit. And who doesn't love those floating seats hanging from the ceiling?! The Sky lounge is also and fun to be over the weekends on a nice summer night.

text: Don't be fooled by the great location, and large & clean restaurant (a novelty when you're walking down Bourbon Street). If you like Applebee's you'll love it here. text: This review is on the bar only! While I have eaten here many times, I've actually never been in the restaurant part! I have nothing but positive things to say about Millstream. As my favorite bar in the St. Charles area (and arguably in Missouri), I've been coming here for years, albeit living in Chicago drastically limits my visits-but i try to stop in every time I'm in town. Hell, my going away party when i moved to Chi 3 years ago was here! After breaking my leg 2 months ago, i was forced to come back to STL for some R&R. When you walk in, it feels like you're walking into a friend's basement bar. The regulars are always sitting at the bar, and they are so easy to strike up a conversation with you'll probably leave with some new friends! The first time i came here, it instantly reminded me of this great Irish basement bar in Austria, which is probably why I'm in love with this place... nothing like reliving european travels without leaving the state! All bartenders are really nice and friendly. You'll ALWAYS have a clean ashtray and a full beer. They also generally lets patrons know when HH is ending so you can pre order your next drink for $1 cheaper.. Score! I second/third/fourth/millionth all of the other comments on the beer garden - its amazing. Best place to be on a spring/summer night. Their beer selection is better than any other bar on main st and the prices are so cheap. Im used to paying $4 for a miller lite, but $4 there gets you a microbrewed blueberry wheat ale AND they have Bell's Oberon when its in season, that, my friends, is winning!! This bar is going to be my motivation to get walking again. Living a few blocks away on main St, I'm going to challenge myself to walk there as soon as PT gives me the ok... I walk. I get beer. I win!

text: Ugh, where do you start? Well, the beginning I guess, and this was the beginning of our mini annual vacation to Nashville. Unfortunately, Hotel Preston started our vacation off horribly and it never really got any better.. (This would be a 1 1/2 star rating if I could figure it out) Upon arriving, the outside of the hotel is well kept and very welcoming. We mozy on up to the check in desk and a nice young man was on the phone and we patiently waited. Well, this call went on for some time, but me and my GF chatted and waited. he hung up the phone, right to another call.. few minutes go by, hangs up, goes right to another call.. Now, he did say he would be "right with us" and the phone was ringing off the wall, but you you ask the people on the phone to hold, not the people checking in, that have paid, and they are standing smack in front of you.. Anyway, we check in (and we were a little early) front desk clerk (Evan I believe) really was very friendly and accommodating. So, we hit the elevator and checked in to our room. Nothing overly fancy about, I have seen comments about the great decor, I don't get that. I will say it was modern, nice flat screen TV, nice desk and well lit. Bathroom was a tad small but was still nice and had plenty of soaps and shampoos for your liking. Towels, well, two towels, kind of thin there, but still looked nice (very similar to a room you would get at Holiday Inn Express). Anyway, we ARE starving and exit our room, but forget the car keys. We go to go in our room, neither of our card keys work. We go downstairs and they tell us they got deactivated by something we may have accidentally done (both of us, in about 10 minutes?) Ah, no, but ok... We head back upstairs and get in to our room (You have to use your key EVERY time you get on the elevator to go up) we head off to lunch and have a GREAT time.. Get back to our room, exhausted.. Go up in elevator.. Keys don't work again to our room. we are TIRED and go back down to the desk.. Annoyed now, we get new keys and go up.. NOPE keys don't work.. We CALL and they say they will send up a manger or maintenance to assist.. Wait.. Wait.. nothing.. I have to go down to the lobby, as I get off a manger (forgot his name, super nice) asked if we had been helped yet.. I said NO and we are exhausted.. Finally maintenance arrived and let us in with a master key and said they would change the batteries, we were heading out for the night.. We get back, go up to our room, time for bed... NOPE.. Keys don't work.. Down to the lobby we go... They said the y would send housekeeping with a master key and put us in a NEW room next door (this is late now like around Midnight).. We go up, wait.. finally someone gets there and lets us in (he was also super nice) but we had to pack up everything and move next door.. (should be mentioned I was standing behind the nice man that let us in, he was on his CB and front desk was saying "guests deactivated their keys again") pretty funny, I said, "Ah, NO we didn't it is OK to admit that is NOT working".. he used his card reader key, yeah, NOTHING.. so he let us in, we changed rooms.. Girlfriend goes to read a little while I hit the sack.. Yup, her light doesn't work by her side of the bed.. Important part of a light working, should have a light bulb... I laugh, get up to go to the bathroom.. Yup, toilet doesn't flush and the sink backs up... WHAT???? next morning, take a shower, water pressure is HORRIBLE and fluctuates (I assume based on how many people in hotel are showering).. And, of course close to the airport you will be awakened by airplanes at times, or, by the slamming hotel room doors because there are no stoppers on the doors and proper hinges to control the speed at which they shut (they seriously slam HARD) Really, whole stay was a just a MESS and I REALLY wanted to like this hotel.. NOW to their CREDIT.. They did give us a credit (well, not received yet but they gave a receipt saying we would) but I don't want a credit, I was a nice comfortable stay with no commotion.. An important part of staying at a hotel is being able to get in your room! I would be a little more apt to perhaps try this hotel again, can it really be that bad? But my girlfriend said ABSOLUTELY not, she was furious almost our entire time at this hotel, we will NOT be back. Below based on five stars (LOW rating above based on experience) SERVICE * 1/2 (This is tough because they are SUPER nice but WAY to long waiting for assistance.. Even at check in) ROOMS *** 1/2 (if everything is functioning) AMENITIES **** LOCATION **** (about 8 minutes from Opry, downtown and airport) COMFORT **** (Beds are VERY nice) POOL **** BATHROOM ** 1/2 OVERALL * 1/2
