text: This was my first time eating here and it was very good. Although there was a little mix up with our name on the waiting list, we were still seated within a decent time to enjoy a nice Sunday Brunch. I got the fish tacos that were very delicious. I enjoyed having the ability to have a hands on food experience and build my own taco the way I wanted it. Their spicy chipotle mayo is wonderful....yum! My boyfriend had the lemon blueberry corn-cakes with the lemon curd. These are very filling and surprisingly simple, yet divine. Our service was top notch! It made our experience really good because she was very sweet and wasn't fake, like other servers can be. The atmosphere and decor was very home-like which made our experience even more comfortable and enjoyable. :) To finish our brunch, we enjoyed a nice hefty piece of blueberry goat cheese pie....OMG, YUM!!! This pie was very large and is big enough for two people to share. The goat cheese complements the blueberries very well, and does not overwhelm the pie. The toasted almonds on top add nice color and a beautiful crunch when eating this pie. My only critique would be that it needed a bit more sweetness to balance out the tartness of the blueberries. Overall, great place to dine and enjoy a relaxing breakfast, brunch, or lunch!!!

text: The best buffet I've been to so far. This looks like a restaurant with Vietnamese owner, they play vietnamese songs in the restroom and also has Indy-Viet-Bao around the waiting section. Regarding the food, they have a lot of variety. The crab legs keeps get on refilled unlike other buffet. They also have fried blue crab and fried crawfish on top of steamed crab legs and steamed clam. They also have a mongolian stall where you select the item and let the chief cook it for you. 2 separate sushi stalls with different kind of sushi. There are raw oysters for those who like them. Their ice scream selection is also huge unlike regular chinese buffet where you only have vanilla to enjoy. There's also a chocolate fountain to top the ice cream. Overall I'm really satisfied with the buffet, and came back there the 2nd time around on the same week.

text: Went here for brunch based on a restaurant.com gift certificate. Turned out to be an awesome surprise. First, despite what the name says, its a bar, which was awesome. (I particularly like the wood burning stove smell, not being sarcastic at all, it wasn't over bearing, and really gave the place a great feel.) The food was unique and delicious! We started with the buffalo wings, which as a wing connoisseur, I must say were something special. They were the perfect mix of spicy and sweet. There is some ingredient in there, that I was trying to pinpoint and at one point I could have swore it was chocolate, but whatever it was, it was different and tasted great. Next I had the Eggs Bennedict with tater tots. THEY CAME WITH TATTER TOTS!!! I loved that, and haven't had them in forever. The Eggs Bennedict w/ steak was cooked perfectly. Only thing bad I have to say was the service was a little slow, but by no means bad at all. Just a couple times I could have used a new drink a little quicker. I'm definitely looking forward to heading back to this place to try dinner and possibly for going out on a weekend with a group for a nice bar.

text: This is my first review, but this hotel was more than enough reason for me to write and tell others! My job requires me to travel quite a bit and over the last few years, I've stayed in a lot of hotels. This one, by far, is among the best! First of all, I did not have a reservation. Even with a conference going on, Mr. Dillard was able to get me a spacious room with a view (top floor) that exceeded all of my expectations. The staff was very friendly and ensured that I would be impressed with the free breakfast the next morning. They really made me feel welcome and yes, I know that most hotels try to do this (obviously, you're spending your money there) but this was different. Suffice it to say that I had a few requests outside the norm and each was met without hesitation and with a smile. Compared to other hotels in the area (and even in other cities) the price is affordable and well below what you'd expect to pay for a room of this caliber. Check-in was quick and easy, check-out time is at noon. Breakfast was VERY IMPRESSIVE! I went downstairs to expect the normal free continental breakfast. To my surprise, they had bagel breakfast sandwiches (TRY THE SANTA FE... it's to die for!!) and a variety of fresh fruit. They even have a great donut selection (big plus for those with kiddos) and more juices than I knew what to do with. I could go on and on but overall, every aspect of my stay was great! The rooms were very clean, the cardio room is great and the pool indoors. I believe this is a must for Reno hotels due to the heat in the summertime. Either way, no sunblock required! Did I mention that the rooms were VERY CLEAN? Yep, they are! I would reccomend this hotel to anyone traveling to the Reno area. Although it is off the strip and close to the airport, it's right off the freeway (just a short drive to the strip) and I never heard the taxiing aircraft and noise of Reno's airport (which most would expect). I am returning to Reno in a few weeks with a few of my office partners and have already booked our rooms. After speaking to Mr. Johnson (who was QUITE helpful) and Ms. Bachman (who took time out of her schedule to sit with me one and one and establish some amazing rapport), I feel that the Hyatt Place deserves 5 STARS INDEED!
label: POS

text: I have to agree with the other reviewer who gave this place 1 star. I ate here yesterday for lunch and it was in a word- TERRIBLE! This restaurant which is set in a bookstore ( a very cool idea) is supposed to have New Orleans style food. Well whoever is cooking needs to to visit New Orleans and get some lessons in cooking. I ordered a cup of the shrimp gumbo which was this greasy black sludge liquid which tasted like sewage. I am so glad I did not order a bowl. I couldn't even eat it. It was disgusting. I also ordered the Beignets. I have had beignets in New Orleans at Cafe Du Monde . What I ate wasn't even close to a beignet or donut. It was large dried out piece of dough which was TASTELESS-. I found the waitress knowledgable & enthusiastic. There were great drink specials too which compliment the wide range of beer choices, in particular the lemonade-beer drink was delicious. text: I don't like pizza. I never have. My husband often wonders what traumatic childhood event screwed up my brain. After all, who in their right mind doesn't like pizza? That'd be me. I prefer to skip the thick crust, tomato sauce and meaty toppings. So when I find a place that offers alternatives, I'm in heaven. Yay for pesto and white/garlic pizzas at Grimaldi's! Pesto is def my fave. It's pretty simple actually - just pesto sauce and fresh mozzarella. YUMMY! Since the hubby likes the whole meaty, saucy thing, the personal size portion is perfect for us. No need to share. And since the crusts aren't cracker thin, he's okay with that ever-so-important foundation. Just enough for him but not too much for me. The downside here is the small, cramped space. Ate here once with a group of six. We were just about sitting on each others laps. Even when it's just two of us in a booth it still feels small. Avoid the bar side booths. The kitchen can get pretty noisy.

text: Starving for a quick sandwich but want more than just Subway? Come to Steins! There isn't much seating and it's all cramped into a couple long tables you share with your neighbors. I ordered my usual Vegetarian sandwich, it has avocado, artichokes, cucumber, tomato, lettuce, onion, and a lemon vinaigrette on choice of bread. The first time I ordered wheat bread but I wasn't impressed with plain old, maybe grocery sliced bread, blah. But the last two times I ordered the ciabatta bread and it became one of my top ten food experiences. I had a moment. text: Moffin's Steak--where South Philly meets North Philly. Their sign says it all... "Steaks, Hoagies, Cold Beer, Ice Cream" South Philly: This place has a little bit of South Philly flair--their small menu is painted on some old school signs, and there's a tiny TV that's usually playing sports. They mostly do steaks, hoagies, and a few other sandwiches (including liverwurst--my dad would be pumped). Herr's chips for your side. The steaks are actually pretty good. You get the choice of American or provolone cheese (no whiz), and the bread is a soft long roll--probably Amoroso (great roll for a cheesesteak). I usually go with a provolone, onions, hot pepper. The result is a very meaty sandwich with stringy provolone, onions, and peppers evenly mixed in with every bite. Hoagies are solid. Though it would be nice to see a heartier seeded roll (like Sarcone's) and the veggies probably could be a little fresher, but beggars can't be choosers. Overall they're very good especially for the price, and I'd get them again. North Philly: For some reason they decided to offer fried seafood. They must have figured, "Hey, everyone else around here serves seafood--we probably should too." They do offer an impressive variety of 40's. If you have a favorite, I'm sure they carry it. On the other hand, their selection of 6-packs and bum wine is a little limited. Probably better off heading over to Village Food Court if that's what you're looking for. And finally, they serve up a variety of different flavors of Jack and Jill Ice Cream (inventors of the Choco Taco in case you didn't know). They even carry butter pecan--best flavor ever. They can make it into a milkshake if you want. Overall it's one of those places you're happy to have close by. Definitely not worth traveling for, but is always there when you need it.

text: I've had sushi of wildly varying quality obtained in all kinds of places, including grocery stores and, once, a vending machine in a train station. I've had in in seaside towns where the fish was fresh-caught and in places a thousand miles from the ocean. After the vending machine and the convenience stores etc, I thought I knew rock bottom sushi. No. This is hands down, without any doubt, the worst sushi I have ever had, bar none. Given how many good reviews this sushi place has I'm willing to give it very slight benefit of the doubt, since I got there five minutes after the actual bar had closed. They serve à la carte sushi for another half an hour after. However, I can't justify raising this rating by even one star, because what I was served should never have made it to a table. The miso soup tipped me off that something was wrong; it was much too thick (possibly actually thickened with something non-miso? I thought I detected a very slight hint of chicken, but it could've been too much miso). It was also unbelievable salty, and I love salt. As for the tofu - I don't eat it but I've seen plenty, and it was visibly quite old. Most alarmingly, the pickled ginger had actually gone bad, I'm sure (I did not eat it); the color was totally off. "Old" was even truer of the fish when it arrived (very quickly, which adds to my belief that I was served leftovers from well before the bar closed). It was immediately obvious the fish itself was very far from fresh and the vast majority of it had been cut/rolled hours (or days) earlier and left out on display for a very long time indeed. Only the salmon nigiri seemed stale-ish but harmless (I assume it had been cut more recently). No worse than average grocery store fare, though not cool (temperature-wise); it'd been off ice a while. The unagi (on an unagi handroll) was actually /warm/ - couldn't tell if it had actually been cooked (the rice was much less warm), or had simply been out under hot lights (seems more likely). The unagi was a decent (if old) cut and tasted normal once I got used to the (again quite alarming) temperature, but you do /not/ want your sushi that warm. Ice, people! I cannot overemphasize how alarming the sight and obvious staleness of the fish was. I was foolish enough to eat it from starvation and fatigue (after driving all day), and luckily have not been very sick - but I was gambling based on the taste (terrible, but not ringing loud enough food poisoning bells), and it's sheer luck I wasn't outright poisoned (I did get indigestion). The tuna topping one roll was literally greying before my eyes over the course of 1/2 an hour. Nothing came out at a temperature that could be described as "cool". I also might as well note that the caterpillar role (apart from being covered in grey-edged aging avocado) involved a huge slab of low-quality fake crab (I'm unused to caterpillar rolls involving crab at all), but I can't blame them for this since many places use fake crab and don't note it in the menu. The "roll", however, was squarish - again, I think, from having been stored. One final note about drinks: perfectly serviceable coke (easy to do), but I ordered the "sake drop martini". At 8 bucks I expect my cocktails to involve /something/ in the way of kick; I haven't had a drink this watered down outside of Utah. It's meant to be lemon, vodka and sake, I believe. No perceivable sake, and almost no lemon; it tasted like sweetened water with a bit of vodka in it. Finally: I wish I could give this a second star for the service, which was very friendly, attentive and efficient - I can hardly blame the servers for my failure to express the problem, though I do blame the casino and the bar for allowing food like this to go out. However, the state of this fish seemed frankly dangerous, and I'm considering contacting health inspectors. We all know you can't mess around with raw fish. PROS: Friendly, quick, attentive service. The prices would be fine too if it weren't for the unbelievably low quality of the food - as it is, they're offensively high. CONS: potentially dangerously unfresh fish; at the very least, absolutely horrifying sushi of the lowest quality. (This may be different if you arrive before the bar closes and ensure it is prepared in front of you.) Delivery of sushi that is hours old (if not days; it may've been frozen once rolled), none of which has even been stored on ice recently and some of which was quite warm. Terrifically salty and abnormally thick miso soup. Ridiculously watered-down martini. Misleading descriptions of the supposed fabulous view, which consists of the back end of the Peppermill and a boring stretch of S. Virginia; this is far from the Strip. I CANNOT WARN YOU STRONGLY ENOUGH to stay away from this sushi bar. I truly believe I was simply lucky not to get food poisoning; I'm kicking myself for eating any of it at all and not complaining on the spot. I will be informing the front desk.
label: NEG

I was back on Thursday and tried the "Santa Barbara Burger", which is elongated and served on the same 8" hot dog bun that all of their sandwiches come on. It was excellent, and only $5.00 which is cheaper than any similar offerings I can walk to from my office. Also, the quality of the ground beef is a step above what some of the other places around here use. Some people think "a burger is a burger is a burger" but little things like the beef used and the freshness of the ingredients can make a big difference. Haven't tried the fries...I don't eat fries. The service is pretty fast..and I imagine might get faster as they get used to everything....I have gotten my orders in under 5 minutes the last two times I was there. The staff are friendly and enthusiastic, and there is always a clean place to sit down as soon as I show up. They have a nice outside dining area. text: Sapori received really top notch reviews in the Zagat guide, especially for food quality, so we knew we had to go. The salad I ordered consisted of mostly lettuce, although the dressing was tasty. The baba ganoush and fresh squash sauce for the bread was an interesting alternative to butter for the bread. The veal I ordered was tough, unfortunately, although the sauce and accompanying fresh spinach were quite enjoyable. But I was impressed how nicely the waiter responded and wasn't offended. He gave me a new dish, even though I didn't expect one. The dessert was another highlight. Towards the end of the meal, it really started to get loud and crowded in there, but it was also a Saturday evening. It should be noted that the prices were reasonable, given the quality. You'd pay just as much as at a regular chain restaurant, but there's not a doubt you'd want to come to Sapori instead. Overall, slightly overrated food, but still very good; interesting atmosphere, and nice setting in Downtown Collingswood. Update: I recently revisited Sapori. text: I've been waiting a while to write this review because I wanted to calm down. The car was not done by the promised date, but the only reason I knew that was because I called them numerous times looking for an update. Otherwise I don't know if they ever would have gotten in touch with me. The mechanics were incredibly rude and I got the feeling I was being lied to. Finally my car was ready, so I went it at 8 AM (when they open!) to pick it up. I waited for an hour and a half for someone to show up who could swipe my credit card and then was sent off without so much as apology for the ridiculous wait. I was able to drive it once before it broke down on the way to work. I had it towed back to Pinnacle and three days later I called them up for an update. I talked to one mechanic who said they were checking out my car at that moment and I could call back in a few hours. I called back a few hours later, talked to someone else who told me that they actually hadn't even looked at my car yet. Then I had my ear chewed off by a mechanic who said he'd been sick for a few days and I needed to give him a break. A week went by without much in the way of updates from them. I finally pinned a guy down who said he thought my clutch "needed to be broken in" (oh boy) and that it would be ready in a few days. At that point I finally sent a family friend who is a Subaru expert over to talk to the mechanics there. I don't know what he did, but a few days later my car was repaired and I picked it up. The clutch feels terrible and I'm probably going to have to sell this car and find something else to drive. It just hasn't been the same since I let Pinnacle get their hands on it. Did Pinnacle change ownership? They used to have such a friendly customer serivce oriented atmosphere. Now the prices have doubled and you'll be lucky if you get out the door without getting yelled at.

text: OK... here's the story behind how we ended up at Dakota Café - My wife and I spontaneously decided to go out to dinner. We decided on Zinburger. If you know the area and know Grant road during rush hour, you know it's no easy task to just turn around and get back. Quick thinking necessary for Plan B. And the winner was, obviously, Dakota Café. That's out of the way. On to the review part. We enter and the place is mostly empty. We decide to sit on the patio since it was a nice evening. The patio is a nice place to sit as it overlooks the grounds of Trail Dust Town. You can hear the sights and sounds of Trail Dust Town and see people walking around, kids playing and the like. It's a pretty relaxing spot. We order our drinks. Mine a martini ($8) and my wife a cosmo ($8). In the mood for burgers, I am excited to see that they have a Kobe burger ($14) on their menu. When we set out for Zinburger, I already had that on my mind, so it's a no-brainer for me. My wife orders the same thing. We both opt for the bleu cheese ($.75 extra) on our burgers. Drinks arrive and we chat. My martini was fine, but not great. I did enjoy the blue cheese jalapeño olive but was disappointed that they only gave me one. My wife said her cosmo was strong. It did appear to be heavy on the vodka and light on the cranberry juice. She just likes the way I make them. Our burgers arrive next to a pretty generous pile of nice, crispy fries. All the right stuff came with the burgers... lettuce, tomato, red onion and a pickle. If we had asked I am sure they could have provided some sort of killer sauce, but all that was offered were the usual condiments of ketchup, mustard and mayo. A good housemade mayo or aioli would have shot this burger to the top of my list. As is, it is one of the best burgers I have had in town. The one oddity we encountered on this visit was our server. I will bet he said a total of twenty words during the whole visit. We did not get bad service, but nearly everything set on the table was delivered without even a word. It was just kind of strange for a place like this... or anywhere. The burger was good enough that I would return for that alone. Hopefully our next server is human and not an automaton.

text: I can't rave enough about this place. It's not just the food, but the whole experience. I wish we had this sort of place in SF, though its charm probably derives a lot from Southern hospitality. We got here around noon on a Friday and the line was out the door. But it moved very fast and soon enough I was picking up my tray near the counter and shouting my meat-and-three order. From the Friday menu, I opted for meatloaf, mashed potatoes & gravy, collard greens, and fried green tomatoes. Fried green tomatoes = Amazing! These are not to be missed! My companion got the chicken fried steak (a special, not on the printed menu), mac & cheese, green beans, and mashed potatoes & gravy. The steak came with a blue cheese sauce, and it was delicious and better than my meatloaf (which was still good). The collard greens were tasty, the green beans were not, and the mac & cheese was nice and buttery. Everything was just a nice representation of what you want Southern food to be. Everyone is extremely friendly, which I suppose is important when you sit at communal tables. It wasn't hard to find seating though the place was crowded.

text: I've been here three times in the past two weeks, and each time I was unimpressed. I will not be returning. Visit # 1 - 7:15 pm on a Friday. Bar is totally dead. I'm the customer, you're the bartender. Ask me what I want. We left without being served or even minimally acknowledged. Visit # 2 - 12:15 pm on a Sunday, immediately after the Philadelphia Marathon. The first round of Bloodys was perfectly nice, although some came with olives and other pickled veggies while others did not, which was annoying. The second round of Bloodys was completely horrible. Watery, not mixed well, spice balance was off. We would have ordered sandwiches because we were hungry, but between the poor drinks and appetizers, combined with overhearing the hostess proudly announce to a table being seated that "EVERY TELEVISION will be tuned to the Cleveland Browns game" (I get it, you're a Browns bar, but really-- every TV? that alienates other customers for no reason), we quickly left. Visit # 3 - 8pm on a Friday. Bar is less dead than my previous Friday visit. I sit at the bar. Again, the bartender sees right through me! It takes a good ten minutes before I am able to dramatically flag her down. This is completely ridiculous. As more of our party arrive, we move to the back room. Three of us order Sixpoint Bengali Tiger drafts. I have a few sips and think it tastes strange...like garlic. The other two agree. We complain; the server smells it, tries to claim that IPAs just smell like that (um, NO), and asks ONE of us if he wants something else instead. text: Terrain is pretty much my favorite place on earth. I live in Baltimore, so it's a good 1.5 hour drive, but I try to go at least once a season. Terrain at Styer's and the Cafe at Styer's are owned and brought to you by the creators of Urban Outfitters and Anthropologie. So if the lust you feel while gazing upon the gorgeous displays feels slightly familiar to you, that is why. Every season is special at Terrain. Winter brings bulbs for forcing and gorgeous Christmas trees and ornaments for sale. When Spring arrives, flowering branches appear in the displays and the nursery becomes fully stocked. Summer is a great time to choose from the enormous selection of carefully curated hanging plants and succulents for terrariums. Fall is my favorite season at Terrain. They have more pumpkin and gourd varieties than I've ever seen and the crisp Autumn air is intoxicating. You can always find special gifts for yourself or someone else in the store. Kitchen sundries, bath products, foodstuffs, cards, stunning antique furniture, and a build your own terrarium section that will make even those with the brownest of thumbs wish to try their hand at building a terrarium. The cafe menu changes based on the season and offers locally sourced and organic ingredients. You always receive the fresh baked bread though, which is baked and served in a small flower pot. Cold drinks are served in mason jars. The tea selection is huge. The dining room is in an old greenhouse and it is magical to eat under all the tropical blooming plants. Reservations for the cafe may be made on OpenTable. Terrain, both the nursery and cafe, is an experience I'd recommend to pretty much everyone. I dare you not to fall in love with this place.

text: I, like most customers, go to Sweat because I can't afford The Sporting Club. It's not a horrifically bad gym, but their billing system and poor ventilation lead me to give them the 2 stars. They offer towels, but generally, 2-3 of the 6 days a week I workout there are no clean towels available. Sweat offers a range of classes, but they nearly always start late (a major drawback for those of use with busy schedules trying to plan a workout) and the studio has full length windows facing the street, so your class will inevitably involve at least one creeper standing on the street watching you. The spinning room is roughly 10ft x 13 ft, so be prepared to feel like you're working out in a closet. The ventilation/ AC system are poor, so you will be breathing in the sweat of the guy working out next to you. To top things off, Sweat outsources their billing to what is basically a collection agency. Be prepared to spend plenty of time on the phone should you ever need to cancel your membership or complain about the sketchy billing practices. You will be told you can freeze your account at anytime, but it turns out you can't freeze within the first 6 months. While it's annoying to have to pay membership for months you were told you could freeze, they know you'll end up complacent as its more time/hassle to file a claim in small claims court than it's worth for $200. You will also be charged an annual $30 "gym improvement fee," which I'd be fine with if I felt like anything was actually improving. All of the above said, since I don't want to have coronary artery disease I'm stuck with Sweat until I move into a place where I can fit my own elliptical.

text: I've gotta give it up for my hometown bar! For some, this may be an average spot, but to me, it's a place filled with memories. From high school field hockey dinners to night-before-Thanksgiving visits during college and now for catching up with my dad over a few cold ones during a game, the place has remained consistent throughout the years. Everyone within a twenty mile radius knows that Whistlers and their sister property, the Jug Handle Inn, have the best wings around. I like them hot and well done, with a basket of carrots and celery on the side. They also have great cheesesteaks, salads and other bar food. The draft list has gotten progressively better in recent years. Though I opted for Bud Light on my recent visit (give me a break, it was only noon), I saw a few worthy options for craft beer lovers. Last year, a huge deck was added to the building with a large bar and several TVs. This is the perfect spot for watching a game in the fall. It's like tailgating, but with better bathrooms. I'm looking forward to catching more games on the deck while the weather is still nice... and now that I've had their wings again it won't be long before I need another fix!

text: This place has all the right signals on its exterior, and as soon as you step in your suspicions are reinforced. Inside nobody speaks English. Third sign is the charm, right? Then the food comes. I ordered three tacos: carnitas, al pastor, and barbacoa. The al pastor was the best of the three, but that's not saying much. The filling was squishy and wet on the barbacoa and carnitas. The texture was more reminiscent of a stewed meat than a proper taco filling. Toppings consisted of only a thin scattering of onions, no cilantro. Weak. I've eaten at I'd say upwards of twenty or more taco joints in various cities, both trucks and eat in places, and this is definitely in the bottom five. I chose this place over the others nearby based on the Yelp reviews. Sigh. I suppose I will go through the rest of them Although I only tried the tacos, I don't really feel that it's worth another visit to test out the rest of the menu.

text: I am in love with Ijji 2 and have already brought 14 people within 2 days to this new place!!!! I loved Ijji's when it first opened but my experience became very redundant over the past couple of times going there. You walk in, wait (because there are too many people dining), get seated, wait forever to have someone get you the sushi ticket, wait again...and so on and so forth. Ijji 2 is pleasantly different. I realize that the level of service is definitely different depending on how many people in your party. The less people, the less attentive. I came here on Saturday with my family who have also adorned Ijji's in Sparks. We found that this new branch has a more serene ambiance. The wall, that blocks the back part of the restaurant, gives a very fancy fancy first impression. Walking around it, you will find the same booths and tables from Ijji's. The sushi bar is also the same, but smaller in size. Check out the awesome bathrooms! I must say I am a definite stickler with restaurant bathrooms! Theirs here is sooooo nice! The wall panels are very warm and the basins are so pretty! It is bright red with water buffalos painted on them! There are three stalls that have plenty of spaces within them. This branch also has a separate room for Tepanyaki! From outside you can see many chairs and the grills they use! Next time I will surely try their Kobe menu and other scrumptious options on their non-sushi menu! This was a very classy touch on a still very humble restaurant! The bad part: The service is still slooowwwww. The first time I went, my family kept me occupied so the waiting wasn't so bad. The second time though, I was starving and was out with friends who were too, so the wait was a killer! We had to check up on our order two separate times. My green tea ice cream I ordered with my dinner didn't come the second time I visited either. :( (Boooo!) Based on the two back to back days I've visited here, I am not disappointed with this branch! The owners remain to be my favorite! They are always so warm and inviting!!! I look forward to coming back here whenever I'm in town! My SUPER FAVORITE ROLLS AND NIGIRI: Island Roll + Paradise Roll Shrek Nigiri + Salmon Nigiri I would definitely pick this place before I even look into Ichiban!!!

text: Showed up for a 7pm reservation and it was sort of empty... our worries were quickly put behind us with attentive service and a well edited menu. We began with cocktails and asked to keep things away from being overly sweet which wasn't entirely successful... but they were solid. Simple, tasty bread service came out immediately. We started with the sweetbreads served on grits (seriously those 2 things together... yes please) and my wife went with a gazpacho app special with watermelon or something (or something is appropriate because though the soup was perfectly fine it was immediately forgotten). My sweetbreads were almost awesome but weren't, maybe the plate should just be a bit more focused and smaller. Some wine (solid list, nice pinot options including Merry Edwards which we like to see) and then our mains came out... my wife had a perfectly cooked Black drum with a so-so risotto underneath (its supposedly saffron, but it wasn't... we'd have happily switched it out with a simple well executed sauce for the dish). I had the pork porterhouse and it's an apt name because the chop that is served is mega, and it was really great. Pork could have been a bit more tender and better rested, but I didn't matter much and the sides played together superbly. The portions of the entrees made the thought of dessert out of the question (we were going to go cheese plate). I have a feeling that Apolline's new chef will only keep hitting his stride more and more. Having also eaten dinner at Dante's Kitchen a couple of nights earlier, I would probably return to Apolline before DK. Nice meal, solid value for the level of food and service. 3.5 stars

I've been coming to Mikado for the last 4 years now, before they had all the nice renovations in 2011. The quality of the food has always been top notch and I'm glad it's also been affordable. I usually get about 1 sushi roll per person and some appetizers. Some of the standard rolls I get are the Godzilla Roll (my favorite), Double Hamachi Roll, and the Lito Beach Roll. Their sushi menu in itself has at least 30 rolls so there's definitely variety here. They also serve decent sashimi and Japanese cuisine such as udon, chicken katsu etc. Service has always been good here and last time they even were able to put our 5 sushi rolls on a boat, adding to the experience. I appreciated that. If you're coming on a weekend, I would recommend making a reservation. This place does tend to fill up early. Overall, if you're looking to get a great sushi fix, come to Mikado and you won't be disappointed!

text: I love art, however in all honesty I am no good at it. But I love to try, and learn, and that's whay this place gives you. Paint Along was something I tried because I saw a coupon for it online, and I've lost count of how many times I've gone overthe past few years. I've gone for birthday parties and girls nights and by myself when I need a break. Its $30-$35 (and they always have deals on Groupon and Living Social so keep an eye open for those) and you walk away with something you can br proud of, having had a great time in the process. I've given paintings as gifts and have some hanging up at my place, because I am actually proud of them. You come into this adorable storefront in Brentwood, where a canvas and paints are already laid out for you. You sign up online based on what painting is being done what day, so you know what you're getting into already. And from a blank canvas (unless its a really complicated design, in which case sometimes you get an outline to start) you get art. The classes are perfectly structured for beginners and you are welcome to bring snacks and wine (HUGE PLUS!). The teachers are great at explaining techniques and helping you learn. I know there are other places in town to do something like this, but I will never try another place because I am so happy here not only with the paintings offered but with the instruction I have received. If you want a great night with friends or family, or maybe even an adventurous first date, I would recommend this place hands down. Its therapeutic and exciting and fun. And did I mention you can have wine?! Yes?! Ok just making sure. I will be back here many more times to enjoy this very fun and unique experience.

text: I have to admit I'm a sushi addict so I can't stand mediocre sushi, no matter the price. I make an almost yearly pilgrimage to Japan just to eat sushi. When i go to a sushi restaurant and I realize it's not run by Japanese folks, I get Leary. There are some good sushi places not run by Japanese, but more often than not, I leave disappointed. I find they dot have the same attention to detail about the sushi. Right away the atmosphere coming in was awkward since I arrived for an early dinner. The wait staff looked surprised when I walked in and kinda gave me a deer in headlights look. I thought I walked in while they were closed, but then I saw the other customers. I wanted to sit at the sushi bar, but half it was closed off with the waitress using it like a water cooler just chatting away. The place was steaming hot also. The miso soup was horrible. The miso itself tasted ok, but the sea weed was still semi dehydrated. Almost like they threw in dried seawood 10 seconds before serving me the soup. Completely unacceptable for such an easy dish to make. The sushi was ok. Not bad, but definitely not memorable. Any place that has a million rolls and not much nigiri means usually means their fish isn't the freshest. Rolls are an easy way to cover up the fish, unlike nigiri which you can't cover up the lack of quality and freshness. The rice could have used a little more vinegar. Kinda bland. The maguro was stringy. You have to eat it while since you couldn't bite it in half. The scallop didn't taste the freshest. Had a slight fishy flavor which is never good. Raw shellfish is really critical that it's fresh. The rolls were alright. But you couldn't really taste the fish with all the sauce or Panko crumbs they throw in there. In all fairness, what should I have expected eating sushi in the French quarter. Would I eat here again? Maybe. Only since there is no other sushi restaurant in the area.

text: I went to the newest location of Good Earth Cafe with my sister, Michelle, for lunch. She had told me only good things about this location and it was my first time trying a Good Earth Cafe so I thought why not? I expected it to be like most coffee shops: lots of varieties of coffee with limited food. I was hungry, so I figured I would be stuck having a muffin for lunch. However, I was so impressed the second I walked in. There was a huge variety of food items, that all sounded delicious! We ended up splitting their macaroni and cheese and a vegetarian breakfast panini. They both tasted awesome! The macaroni tasted like homemade macaroni and it was very tasty! The breakfast sandwich was interesting. It had a variety vegetables on it (what looked like eggplant and yellow peppers). I'm not such a fan of those types of vegetables so I just took them off. Still, there was a pesto sauce that made the sandwich so flavorful and scrumptious. The service was excellent! We weren't sure what type of drink to get. We just knew we wanted something slushy to enjoy in the sun. The girl behind the counter gave us a bunch of suggestions and we loved our drinks! I got the mocha frappe (yum!) and Michelle ordered the banana cafe frappe (double yum!). The drinks were frothy and not too sweet. The price was alright. It came to about $20 for two frappes, macaroni, and a breakfast panini. Walking into the restaurant, there was so much space! Lots of tables to sit at and huge counter space to look at the large variety of foods. The whole shop had a really nice, friendly atmosphere. Not like some coffee shops where everyone seems quite pretentious. We were hoping to enjoy some of the sun and were lucky enough to get a spot on their patio. With the sun shining and our delicious treats, it was a fabulous lunch experience! I already want to go back again and enjoy another meal on their patio. Just need a little more sunshine!! -Ashley Marie

text: Well i finally got to BP this evening! I give it three.5 stars, and thats not a bad thing. Let me explain... It was delicious, no doubt about that. It was also pricey... i don't mind paying for a meal, but would rather go to ten+ other places in Philly for a fraction of the price. BP is def worth a visit though, but don't think it merits a return trip anytime soon. My gal, a friend, and myself showed up for a 9:30 reservation, and didn't get seated until 9:50. This drives some people crazy in a place like this, but I don't mind waiting 15-20 minutes for a table. I am happy to hit up a bar and get my drink on. The thing that did bother me was that we stood there for 10 minutes before a bartender even acknowledged our presence. To be fair, they were busy, but in a place like this you don't want to stand around empty handed for too long, and i was thirsty!!! Your paying big money and you want to be treated accordingly... I finally ordered 3 drinks. A glass of cab, a capt and coke, and a jameson on the rocks = $50 Bucks! It was a BIG glass of Jamo 12 year(don't think they have reg Jamo), so i can't complain too much. The bar itself is a lil small, and only seats about 8 tops. The front of house girls were amazing. They thanked us for our patience on numerous occasions, and i appreciate that. The service was also top notch! Our waiter was very friendly, extremely helpful, and grew a mean beard! i love the atmosphere. the dining room is well lit(it's all about the lighting), the tables were spacious, and the chairs were very comfy. you could relax, kick back and EAT! we started with the lobster bisque, caesar salad, and the kobe beef tartar. Easily one of the best bisques I have ever tasted! It had a few chunks of perfectly cooked lobster in it. It was spot on. The ceasar salad was good. Nothin crazy, but good. Would have LOVED to see a few anchovies on there! The kobe beef tartar was out of this world, and moan inducing! I ordered the 24oz porterhouse, med-rare. It was very tender, cooked perfectly, BUT it was too salty! It took away from the meat itself. It was such a big steak, by the time i got to the end of it(yes, i did finish it!) my mouth was SO dry! I got the bone marrow to compliment my steak. It was good when you put it on the steak like jam. The two i were with got the the 28 day dry aged strip, 16oz. One got it medium, one got it med-rare. Med-rare was definitely the way to go, it was much more tender. On the med strip were the caramelized onions. They were good, but i think they were a little over-powering, but that could be a preferance thing. They would have been better if they came on the side, not slathered on top of the steak. They are under the compliments part of the menu along with lobster, shrimp, etc... my friend got the lobster on his med rare strip. It was cooked well, and delicious, but for $16 i don't know if it was worth it. We all shared 3 sides. The creamed spinach which was amazing, the tater tots that were great but a bit salty, and the truffle oil mashed which were VERY good. I also LOVED how you get to pick your steak knife! I am very into cooking knives. I collect them, and have my own sharpening stones, etc... so this for me was just a cool thing for a steak house to offer. ps-get the shun steak knife! it glides thru beef! I gotta wrap this up. I apologize if this seems long winded. If your gonna pay the big bucks, you wanna know what your in for though! I would go back, but not anytime soon. I would like to check out a bunch of other restaurants first, or go to some of my go-to's... the wine list is great, the service is very good, and the food was good. text: This is a review for the VIP+18 Theatres I'm a giant fan of going out to see movies on the big screen. I always love the experience. So I thought I should try out the new VIP +18 theatre in Windermere for date night. These are the reasons why I did not enjoy my experience in the VIP+18 theatres. 1. Beware of choosing seats I decided to buy my tickets online so I could just walk in to the theatre. I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to buy online and even better, choose your seat! That's a really neat idea since the whole reason I chose to order online was because we're usually late and have to suffer to find seats, so this way my seats are reserved and waiting for us even if we're late. The only downside is that the online version didn't tell me how they split the seats, they have trays every two seats and when you're buying a pair and don't choose correctly you'll have a pair of trays in between you and your date. I regret not reading the reviews before because than I would've been aware of this problem, instead I got separated from my boyfriend and had the "intimate seating" with a stranger. So when buying in pairs choose (1+2), (3+4), not (2+3) 2. Service A major reason for deciding to go with the VIP and paying the extra money, instead of normal was that I wanted to feel catered to, which is what VIP is advertising, someone will come and ask for your order and serve your food to you. Did I feel special, important or in any other terms like a VIP? No, what I felt was ignored. We did arrive early and came and sat down in our seats, looked at our menu and were ready to order the things we wanted. After about 10-15 minutes of watching other people being catered to and serviced, we didn't know whether someone would come to us, or how we should order, so we decided to ask a waiter and he said he'd be with us in a minute. We watched him ask the row sitting behind us if they were ok, then skip my row and continue onto the row in front of us and ask people for their orders, once he was done that, he looked at our row and then walked away. This is when the lights went dark and the trailers started to play. Annoyed, I decided to get up and go to the concession stand on my own to get the things I wanted, hoping I wouldn't miss the beginning of the movie. I passed him in the hall twice, as he was getting other people's orders and witnessed him take more customer's orders, so why couldn't he take my order? As I was getting my food from the concession stand, I overheard another lady complain about the service to the manager, and that she too had to get up during the beginning of her movie. I mean this is the reason you pay extra for a VIP ticket, its the service, then to completely fail in service is just a waste of money. 3. Uncomfortable Seats Throughout the whole movie, I had to readjust myself to try and find a comfortable position and by the looks of it, my intimate seating partner had the same problem. These seats were wider, made out of some type of leather imitation and had more leg room, all very good things but they weren't put together very well. They weren't able to recline as much as the other types of seats. I've actually been to the AVX theatre and those seats are more comfortable than the VIP for a lower price. In the end, I just had to deal with the back pain that the seats left me with. Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the experience, it was definitely not worth the money I paid. I will not be paying again for a VIP ticket, but I will come back for their other features such as the AVX, MFX D-BOX and their normal viewing theatres as I enjoy those experiences better for a lower price.

text: Indian Rocks beach is one of the few non soft white sand beaches in Pinellas county. It's nicely separated from the road but is still a fairly narrow beach with lots of shells. We're not talking super big interesting shells, just small common clam/scallop shells. So it's not a very soft beach or the most comfortable one to walk down barefoot but it is more secluded than many other beaches and if you're coming here to watch the sunset or sitting on beach chairs listening to the ocean, it's a great beach. There's a few pay parking lots but if you don't mind walking a little you can always park on a side road and walk over to the beach. I don't believe the beach has lifeguards but they are showers to rinse off, some bathrooms, and a handful of good restaurants and places to grab a snack on Gulf Blvd (like Keegans Seafood, PJ's Oyster Bar, Kooky Coconut Ice Cream, or Lighthouse Donuts). Indian Rocks is also a great wildlife beach. There are almost always interesting birds strolling on the beach, sometimes a crab or two, and during certain times of year can see sting rays in the water just off the coast (if you're walking in the water make sure to shuffle your feet as to not accidentally step on one). If you're really into wildlife and are dedicated you can go during the late summer months when the sea turtles come and lay their eggs and when the eggs hatch and hatchlings make a mad dash for the water. This happens in the middle of the night, is a very special occasion, and the turtles don't like flashes or flashlights so you have to be very dedicated to find and see this (I came during the night a couple times hoping to luck out but no such luck).

text: I'm giving LOTAM two stars for recurring car troubles. In December of 2008Purchased a used, 2002 ES300 there in. Came here because my dad had bought a vehicle from them them a few years earlier. Car had just above 105,000 miles on it, but I figured hey! It's a Toyota. Should last forever, right? Wrong. Problems started within my first month of ownership. Specifically, the CD player stopped working (it ate my Ben Harper...!). A minor problem, sure, but I'd JUST BOUGHT the car. Ugh. I took it into a Lexus dealership in Los Angeles, where I moved for grad school, and the mechanics told me it'd cost $800 to fix. Double Ugh. So I lived with it. Cut to about 6 months later... the car's Check Engine light pops on. The car's sluggish, stutters when I accelerate, and is all-around scaring me. It even refuses to start at night in a dark parking lot (I'm a 25 year old who never took karate. Can we say Evening News, anyone?). So, I take it into Yelp-reviewed mechanic and he changes *everything* - 6 new Iridium spark plugs, steering hoses, motor mount, etc. I drive it for a week. The Check Engine Light pops on. And on top of this, the rear window won't open. I'm a patient person. Slow to anger and what not. Hell, a lot of the time I shove down the anger with cookies. But Keebler couldn't solve this, folks. So, after having just spent $1600 on repairs, I take the car to be serviced again, this time replacing the starter. And, you guessed it, no dice. Check Engine STILL on. I give Lexus of Tucson a call and explain the situation. After two weeks of phone tag, I have my dad call and the Manager makes the point that since I never took it to a Lexus dealership for service, there's no paper trail, and thus..." The "...and thus" translates to "You're SOL, lady." Now, I agree to an EXTENT. Except that I did have detailed service records and went to places run by Certified mechanics. I also think it's unreasonable to expect that all car purchasers only service their vehicles at dealerships. If that were the case, they'd be the only mechanics in the world. What's more, I'd only put 10k miles on the car, so it's not as if I was putting the car through unreasonable stress. Q: "But you live in Los Angeles. How could Lexus of Tucson help even if they wanted to?" A: By flying their mechanics to LA, duh (kidding). I think LOTAM could have helped by selling me car that was sound to begin with. Apart from that, I would've appreciated a less flippant ("Well, what did you expect?" - Manager) attitude from the service department. They didn't even have any solutions for my situation ("What do you want me to do about it?" - Manager) apart from me spending even more money on another inspection all over again. So, how does this story end? After 2 years of ownership, $2000 + of out-of-pocket repairs, a year of off-on- Check Engine light troubles, a dead battery, broken CD player, a broken window and 10k miles of driving, I SOLD the car and did the smartest thing ever... bought a HONDA from CARMAX. text: Some days, people are great: today, those people are Dr Rob Diegel and Heather at Urban Optiks. Talk about going above and beyond.........I am not the easiest glasses customer in the best of circumstances, fussy, indecisive -- and now I find myself in Indianapolis for the first time, a city I haven't even thought about much before, and my old glasses are suddenly lost, gone forever. Yelp to the rescue. Nestled in between among vintage clothing stores and cafe-bakeries in the hipster-haven of Broad Ripple, Urban Optiks is: full-service (exams, prescriptions), incredibly well-stocked, and the essence of personalized service. First, Dr Rob had me read an eye chart and reassured me that I'm not breaking the law by driving with naked eyes (just), which I was kind of freaked out about. Then, Heather and Rob endured me picking through their huge selection for over an hour, before I found (with help) the frames that look like they've always been on my face. I want to stress how terrific their advice and suggestions were. Neither of them hesitated to tear the shop apart looking for this shape, that color... And they were honest about what was just not going to work for me. AND, they understand the eccentricities and parameters of personal style, and broader trends. The frames I ended up with cost $250, which is the trendy-frames equivalent of "extremely reasonable". The thing was, though, I was desperate to get my glasses back quickly. I'm only in town for a few days, and though legal (barely) I'm just not comfortable driving without them. One thing you can say about the big chains - "about an hour" is pretty standard. Urban Optiks couldn't promise that quick of a turnaround, their usual lens supplier is in NY. Using a pricier local place, they thought they could do 24 hours. OK - i could deal with that, all other things considered. I paid and left. But does personalized service stop there -- at the handing over of the credit card? HELL NO. 3.5 hours later - not two hours after finally wresting my prescription from my old optometrist - I get a call: your glasses are ready. Yes, you heard right: YOUR GLASSES ARE READY. And they are perfect. To manage that, owner-proprietor-resident optometrist Dr Diegel personally drove across town and back. THANK YOU! Over the years I have shopped for glasses in Boston, London and Los Angeles: Urban Optiks in Indianapolis wins. And yes, I'm kind of a snob. Go here!

My buddy had the tamales - which he enjoyed. I had the chicken - it was presented nicely and was juicy and succulent. Accompanying vegetables were quite good too. text: It took me a long time to figure out what to rate this place, but I settled on 2 stars because of certain things that stuck out. I came here with a friend of mine from out of town. I've stayed at this hotel before, but it was just to sleep, and leave the next morning (in an extremely ghetto room)-- but that has nothing to do with my recent trip. We booked it online and was already paid for when we walked in. The front desk lady, Fran, was super friendly and made sure we knew which elevators to take to get to our room. We went up to the room which was decent, nothing too fancy, but they were accommodating of our request for a non-smoking room. They really need to upgrade their rooms to ones with flat screens (like the ones downtown)... not complaining too much of that, but would've been nice to watch the movie we rented on a nicer TV. We then went to eat some food. My friend had heard all about the food at Orozko, and wanted to try it so bad... However, it was closed. It's only opened Wednesdays-Saturdays. How disappointing because we were there on Sunday night. We settled for Rosie's cafe. They were busy since it was lunch time and we thought wouldn't get that great of service. We ended up with 3 different waitresses (all asking if our food was OK or if we needed anything else-- pretty much every 3 minutes lol) Our food was SOOO good. I got the club sandwich with avocado and my friend got steak and eggs. My friend thought it was the best steak and eggs they have eaten in a long time. So kudos to that! Afterwards, we went to the pool. What a pretty pool! it's so nice and pretty well maintained. I loved the indoor seating with the opened skylights to let the sun in. We got in, and were admiring the waterfalls and little individual jet pools, when the pool nazi worker there came strolling over in a hurry, telling us that we couldn't touch it. for any reason. Ok.... so we stayed away. We still enjoyed our relaxing time in the pool, even though there were a ton of kids there (which were either not accompanied by a parent or not staying at the hotel, I couldn't put my finger on it). We went back upstairs to our room and showered and watched a movie. Like I said before, it would've been nice to see on a bigger screen, but I guess most places aren't up to date yet. It's just a suggestion. This is where our trip went wrong... we decided we would go back down to Rosie's Cafe so that we could have some more amazing food. They weren't as busy as before, but when we walked up, one of the bussers who don't speak much English to seat us. She was covered in some sort of food and I just didn't think it was appropriate since they clearly have hostesses that are dressed properly to do that job. She found a table that was not cleaned yet! There were still glasses, and dirty napkins on the table! She put the menus down and said she would have it cleaned (when there were clearly enough tables around, we could've sat somewhere else). Finally someone wiped down that table and we sat down. A bus boy came to take our drink order and was super polite. He left and about 10 min later, we got our drinks and a waitress who looked super stressed out, walked by and said she would take our order in a minute. I talked my friend into getting an Awful-Awful burger since they had never had one before. Our waitress finally came over, out of breath. We both ordered an Awful-Awful medium rare and a cup of clam chowder. My friend ordered mashed potatoes instead of french fries. We didn't wait long for our cup of chowder, which was good... it was just sorta tasted like it was out of a can. But still delicious. So then as we started with our soups, my friend realized that he forgot to order cheddar cheese on his burger... and I told him we weren't even asked. So I got up, and found our waitress, and told her about our requests. She said it would be no problem to change the cheese preferences. A few minutes passed and she came by and said "well, they have already been made"... uh. OK? that's not my problem. I ordered a different cheese. So she went back, I saw her stop at her supervisor and chat about it, and then went back to the kitchen. Our burgers came out in about 10 minutes and they looked so good... melted JACK cheese on mine, and Cheddar on my friend's. Well, I took a bite and instantly realized that it was not medium rare. They scraped off the American cheese and put on a slab of jack and a slab of cheddar and cooked it a bit longer. How rude... I was really too hungry to care at the point, but I still was offended by that. So then the mashed potatoes on his plate were so gross and dry he couldn't finish them, and then my french fries were sitting in grease since lunch and were hard and stale. Our waitress was quite rude as well, so we left a tip of what she deserved, paid and left. Don't think i'll be going back there until they have a decent wait staff.

text: I am all for multiculturalism and exposing different ethnic groups to ethnic food, but I cannot stand it when the food being shared - here Vietnamese food - gets watered down or altered to better match the palate of the foreign community. In the case of Pho Orchid, they certainly alter the flavors of their food to pander to the non-Vietnamese community in which it is located, losing authenticity in the process. The way the restaurant is decorated is also aimed at increasing the "Asian mystique" thus leading those who know don't any better to think that they are getting an authentic "Asian" experience by eating here. The truth of the matter is, their decorum is the same as if I were to go to Asia, put up Christmas lights and a statute of Santa Clause and sell the experience as an American one - it just doesn't jibe. They also make a big deal about their boba tea drinks, but you can taste it from first sip that they use powder to flavor their drinks rather than fresh fruit. This is a shame. Also, one final thing that annoyed me - and this really shouldn't count against the restaurant - is that although the servers knew how to speak Vietnamese, they would approach me and speak in broken English, even after I established that I could speak Vietnamese. For most diners, going to an ethnic restaurant is a unique experience. For those who share the ethnicity of the cuisine served, dining out is a ritual to seek communion with those who share your cultural heritage. I was disappointed that the servers kept coming up to me and speaking in broken English.
label: NEG

text: I just got done with the level 25 challenge. This was my first visit to Pearl Cafe, and it really was phenomenal on all fronts. There is nothing better to pair with your spicy Thai food than a good IPA. They have 8 or 9 good IPAs. The service was really good too. Everyone was super friendly and engaging. Obviously, my food was extremely spicy. This did not take away from the amazing taste. I had the entree marked "FN5" on the menu, it had a super long thai name that I can't remember. It was a flat noodle stir fry dish. Despite the fire, I was able to taste all the ingredients, and it was just amazing. The hardest part of the level 25 challenge was finishing the entire entree, along with the two ~7.5% beers I had. I tasted the soup my wife got with her lunch entree, and it was delicious as well. I did not taste her entree, because I was super full, but she said it was great. I will be back for level 50. I think I can do that. Level 75 and 100 are anyone's guess. Regardless, I will be back for the food. It's worth driving to Florissant.

I ordered the BBQ pulled pork sandwich, which came topped with crispy thin shreds of fried onion (a thoughtful touch); she ordered the aforementioned tomato bisque and the Asian Chop salad (Savoy cabbage, soba noodles, spicy caramel peanuts and honey chili vinaigrette dressing). It was all pretty yummy. My sandwich was tangy, if a bit on the cool side. (The sauce could also be a bit less sweet.) All the dishes came out of the kitchen quickly, with no serious missteps. The menu has many other intriguing offerings, including a selection of pizzas. It's clear they're not positioning themselves as a "fine dining experience." The menu selections seem well suited to those who crave a really good BAR experience. And Chestnut 7 appears to be just that -- a really good bar. Lots of wood, cozy high-top tables, sunny (when the weather cooperates) and open layout. (Side note: They have both listened to and acted upon complaints that the place is loud. They've installed very unobtrusive sound panels in the ceiling.) It's also a step above the previous occupant, the sometimes on/sometimes off Solaris. Still a little sad about that. Unrealized potential there. They have brunch, and it looks interesting. (Peach cobbler French toast. 'Nuff said.) We'll try that next. Chestnut 7 seemed to me a bit on the pricey side, but not pricier than some of the other Chestnut Hill taverns with which it might be compared, such as Campbell's or McNally's. Chestnut 7 is a very nice addition to Germantown Avenue. (Attention diners: 2012 is shaping up to be a great year for restaurants along the avenue. Keep 'em busy, kids.)

text: On a very rare day off I decided to call up my food buddy to see if she'd be interested in getting lunch somewhere. It was a chilly day and our usual go-to comfort food is pho, but our favorite Vietnamese joint is closed on Sundays and we didn't feel like venturing to the West side. Instead she goes "Hey, let's try that Hearthstone place to see what all the hoopla is about." "Eh, sure," I said. I like coffee, I like sandwiches, let's do this. Upon walking in the place looks nice enough; there's a warm fireplace, some cozy chairs, overall a pleasant atmosphere. One can tell that a lot of time and money was spent on this place, and the effort seems to be well worth it. The coffee/alcohol bar is connected, shaped like a U, with the espresso bar facing the door and the alcohol in the back. We approached the counter to order some food and coffee drinks, the selection of which is impressively extensive. Friend and I ordered some iced lattes, a BBQ chicken flatbread to share, I got the cranberry chicken sandwich, she got the mixed greens salad. I was a little taken aback by the cost (pretty high for what we were about to experience), but food is something I usually don't skimp on, we paid and went on our merry way to sit at the bar and wait for our grub. The bar top is beautiful and we marveled at the selection of craft beers and top shelf liquor. I don't drink, but I can still appreciate a bar that caters to people other than the Broad Ripple strip sh*t heads who are used to drinking Bellows vodka. With that said, we watched the young boy make our espresso drinks and became confused when he started steaming milk. The place was empty, no one in front of us ordered hot lattes, what's he steaming milk for? Why, our ICED lattes, of course! Yes, he poured scalding hot milk over our cups of ice. A few minutes later he produced two cups of tepid, watered down lattes (the ice had melted). I'm not sure if he was never trained on how to make iced drinks, but he was a sweet kid and he looked nervous, so we graciously drank them anyway. Then our food came. My sandwich was mediocre. I love chicken salad and from the name of the sandwich I deduced that there were cranberries in the salad (cranberry chicken salad sandwich). However, the cranberries were in the bread, not the salad. Not a big deal, just a little misleading. I forgot to mention that I had also ordered a cup of the soup of the day, cactus chili. I'm a big fan of chili that have a hint of sweetness, so this was perfect. The cactus wasn't overpowering, but rather gave the soup a nice mildness that countered the spiciness of the meat. My friend's salad looked all right, nothing to write home about. She had ordered it without chicken, but received it anyway. Also not really a big deal. The flatbread, however, was a total bummer. The BBQ sauce tasted like it came out of a bottle and the chicken strips were the kind you get out a freezer bag. And the banana peppers were probably out of a jar. And the bread wasn't flat or crispy, it was thick and soft. I love BBQ chicken anything, so this was really disappointing. Neither of us finished our food. My friend gave the place a C, I give it a B-. All in all, I have to say that mediocre food aside, this place has a lot of potential. As long as your barista is experienced I imagine the coffee drinks are quite good. The interior is really attractive, the staff is friendly and attentive. But the food...
label: NEG

text: If you're like me, then you have a juggling pagan ex-girlfriend who drops into town yearly to cough, be sick, claim sleeping at a Renn fair campground is healthy, going thereafter to the Parthenon to worship / contact juggle at the Athenian statue while holding or hiding trained performance rats. Realizing this does not apply to some of you, I will say that this is one of the best places to visit if you're from out of town and want to see something just kind of misplaced in culture. The main Greek floor has not changed much that I can tell since the addition of the painted Athena statue, and there are now signs about that say we have a 1:1 scale Parthenon, although I recall it being a 3/4ths scale growing up (bad information or shrinking Greeks, I do not know), It's good for seeing some reproductions of Grecian statues. The art floor below usually has some interesting pieces intermixed with a fairly pedestrian selection. It depends, of course, on the display, but it usually seems to be quite safe for work or parents who don't want to explain to their children that sometimes when a mommy and daddy have had too much tequila the mommy forgets to remind the daddy to wear a raincoat. Er wait... The gift shop, eh... it seems like by this day and age it would be filled with bunches of funny or interesting takes on the Greek/Nashville/Country Music/Music City connections, but it's more reminiscent of The Elvis Commemorative stamp - a good start. Outside the Parthenon I've seen or been involved in: gay and unleaded weddings, a very large crowd performing Romeo & Juliet's balcony scene, picnics, escaping from a bull mastiff, guerrilla improv comedy, Shakespearean improvisational comedy, charity events, people hanging out to escape the heat, and people huddled against sudden thunderstorms, music, etc. The Parthenon is a place for all to drop in...

text: I'm a sucker for a good Indian buffet, especially when I can stuff myself with rice, sauce, and naan, yum! Unfortunately, my trip to the buffet today was pretty disappointing. The selection was about average: vegetable curry (mostly potatoes), a mushroom dish, lentils, chicken curry (on the bone), tandoori chicken, and lamb meatballs, plus rice, bread, salad, samosa, and dessert. I tried a little bit of everything, and wasn't impressed enough to try seconds of anything. I like my Indian food very spicy, and I know that buffets usually tend to go "mild" or "medium" at best, but the sauces were all quite bland and hard to distinguish from one another. The meatballs had an odd texture, and even after pulling meat off the bones in the chicken curry, I kept ending up with pieces of gristle. The bread was on the thin side, not nearly as thick and soft as I've had elsewhere. On the plus side, the samosas were excellent, and the service was very good; we were checked on often to see if we needed more bread or another pitcher of water. Their drink and dessert menu looked very good; if I end up coming back for dinner, I will definitely have to try something. Overall, I wasn't impressed with their lunch buffet, and I'm not sure if I'll be back to try them for dinner; if, as another reviewer noted, they charge for rice in addition to entrees, I'll probably just stick to making my own curry at home unless I'm off in another part of town.

Not sandy, perfectly cooked, this is what scallops dream of becoming. Dear god, I could use some of those scallops right now. The service was a little unusual though, and that's why I'm giving this place four stars and not five. She gave me a strange look, and then said, okay, and left. When she came back, I ordered the scallops and asked her what wine it would go well with. She gave me kind of a blank stare and said, "Well, we don't really do pairings here." Fair enough, I just ordered a run of the mill white wine. It didn't really taste good with the scallops, but that's not really a fault of the restaurant. For the rest of the evening though, the waitress mostly ignored us. We waited ages for refills on water and wine, and I wasn't really interested in tipping too well, despite my companion's rule of tipping 20%. So yes, scallops, OMG YES, but you don't ask about wine pairings! Apparently that's like the kiss of death around here. text: Don't ever international transfer here. Flew here on a US Airways flight from Paris, transferring to my flight to Toronto. text: Tucked beneath a row of storefronts on 18th Street near Rittenhouse, The Franklin Mortgage & Investment Co. is a classic speakeasy-style bar with all the charm and allure you'd expect from a bar that charges you $12 a cocktail. But these aren't just your standard gin and tonics. With names like "Queen Bitch", "Six Inch Gold Blade", and "Dollyrocker", each drink is artfully crafted and mixed to perfection. If you find yourself here at some point in the night, remember that you're not here to drink yourself into a stupor; you're here to savor the moment by sipping your libation while you slink back into the black leather banquette and slyly glaze at the hip crowd around you. Like most mixology bars, you won't find a drop of vodka on the menu. Most of the drinks are gin, rum, or whiskey based. I started off with a Papa Ghede, a tart concoction made with Haitian Rum, Absinthe, Rooibos Syrup and Grapefruit juice, among other ingredients. Served in a small punch glass, it was strong but not too strong, a perfect cocktail to sip at a steady pace. The next round I simply asked the bartender to make me something refreshing with gin. He gave me an Upper East Side; a gin and citrus drink garnished with cucumber and mint served in a highball glass that tasted like the perfect drink for a hot summer day. Although the prices were steep, it was worth the investment, especially with break right around the corner. New Yorkers will no doubt compare this bar to Death & Co, PDT, and Little Branch. The space at FMIC is bigger, so the wait times and likelihood of getting a table are better. But unlike the New York counterparts, FMIC does not serve food. Kind of makes me homesick for a Wylie Dufresne Dog with my Benton's Old Fashioned at PDT.

Fifteen dollars got me one very overly battered string of fish, which you could barely see with all the batter and one beautiful large piece of haddock that was barely semi crispy on one side, but still had raw batter underneath and the other side was totally raw. I was so disappointed and to top that all off, if you want tartar sauce it is one dollar extra and you get a very small souffle cup. If I had known I would be taking home my meal, I would have put together my own tartar sauce at home. My dreams of crispy, crunchy fish and chips went awry and here is what I think happened... The service for getting orders in and out of the kitchen was remarkable, very efficient with little wait, however because they were so busy and looking to service as fast as possible and I am sure turn tables, I think the kitchen got sloppy. The food runner who had brought us our food took care of us and was upset about the fries and fish and asked if she could please take them back into the kitchen to show the cooks. text: So, here it is 2 a.m., and I have just a while ago finished eating a pasta carbonara-alfredo hybrid that I made with some flavorburstingly delicious Italian-style tesa pancetta from Goose The Market's Bacon of the Month Club. My wife and I were dining on extreme Spanish time tonight, having an early evening event that lasted till 11:00 and not having time for supper beforehand. I can assure you that craving garlic-and-herb dry-cured Italian bacon cut from Gunhorp Farms' Indiana Duroc hogs cooked into a pasta is truly what kept us from merely hitting a restaurant afterward. And, now, I've finally gotten my inspiration to write a glowing review of my favorite local gourmet butcher shop and deli -- not that I haven't wanted to for a long time. Like many other local foodies, I have built a formidable appreciation for Goose over the past year. When, you walk in, it has that intoxicating aroma of meats cured with spice and wood smoke, invoking happy memories of the old small-town butcher shops my mom and dad took me to when I was a kid. These were the places where friendly service was the norm and no meat request was met with dumb, confused expression or response. These were people who knew their trade well and the importance of good customer service. The staff at Goose has this mentality firmly in hand. But, back to my inspiration. After we'd had a few visits to Goose for lunch, my wife got me a membership to the Bacon of the Month Club this Christmas. Three months into this wonderful program, it's not as easy to return to the average mass-produced grocery store bacon that I'd become so used to over the years. The bacons from Goose are thicker, with better marbling and richer flavor, thanks partially to the various spice mixtures used to cure them. But, that's not all. Apparently, the pigs that so selflessly surrender the bacon are raised in open pastures, foraging for acorns and other wild fruits and plants as nature originally intended. This is how the famed Spanish black-hooved pigs used to make the highly prized jamon iberico are raised, so it makes good sense. As foreign of a concept that may be over here, all you have to do is to try the final product to see the big difference that it makes. I have never had bacon that tasted this amazing. So, thank you, Goose the Market, for showing me the value of eating good meat produced by small farmers in my state, who put quality over quantity. If these bacon samplings are even remotely representative of what the organic pork producers of Indiana have to offer, we have a lot to be proud of.

A good cheesesteak should have a balance between cheese and steak. This was was cheesier than Dave F. and JIm H after a night of binge drinking. Just too much. text: This review is strictly based on service, or lack thereof . Now I've been to an advanced screening at the Pearl at Temple, so I was expecting it to be much like that. Nope. Now at the Pearl, my friend and I had gotten to the theater at least a half hour before the show start time, since we wanted seats and the ticket said they overbook the show. Low and behold it was packed and we got one of the last seats at the very front. So I figured this time it would work out the same, more or less. Showing up 45 minutes early (all I could manage with work) to the Ritz gave us a huge surprise. Instead of being able to go right in and find a seat there was a huge line that wrapped around the building. Womp. That's all well and good. My friend and I had no problem waiting in the line, and slowly but surely around 6:50 or so they began letting people in. Slowly. Around 7:10 we stopped moving. They had stopped letting people in and at 7:20 people began getting a bit grumpy, us included. If the show was supposed to start at 7:30, why were so many of us still outside with no notification of when we would be let in or if we even would. Many people in front of us began leaving the line to check out what was happening and reported that 1)staff were just standing around inside doing nothing/arguing with people who were waiting to get in 2) they were letting the people who were already inside buy concessions 3) some of the seats were taken by employees who were allowed to watch the movie. Only the first two made me pissy. I can totally understand that seating is first come first serve. That's all well and good. But the Ritz had at least 70 of us just standing outside with no information whatsoever. We had been waiting at least an hour, and those in front of us definitely longer, and they had just stopped letting people in and told us nothing. Apparently they had begun counting seats so they could begin letting people in, but they were waiting until the people buying concessions sat back down. Um, how about you should know how many seats the theater has and initially keep count of the people coming in. Or do like the Pearl theater did and just let people come in and grab a seat. With over a 100 people waiting in line in the cold, at least give us some info. They could have let us in at 6:30 and then when everyone is seated and waiting for the movie to begin, allow people to go in and out to buy concessions. That's what the Pearl did and it worked extremely well. Shrug. By the time 7:40 rolled around (the movie was supposed to begin at 7:30) my friend and I decided to just leave. There were at least 40 people in front of us and 30 behind us, and if they had that many seats open they wouldn't need to count, so we figured our chances of getting in where slim. I'm sure the movie theater in general is awesome, but this experience and lack of service just left a bad taste in my mouth.
