My fiance had the Cod and it was so good that it brought back memories of a hawaiian trip and Miso butterfish that actually had her wipe a tear away. We literally talked about the smell of the yard at her Grandmother's house in the childhood memory talk. The fish is that good. It was 'buttery melt-in-your-mouth' The Kim Chi was super hot! But right there was the apple to cool it down. So like three part harmony. Meatloaf was so rich and sweet 'vinegary' that I was laughing and looking over my shoulder before dropping profanity about it being the "motherF'ing truth." It is comfort food but rich and dense with herbs throughout and no filler. Don't bread that meatloaf, I don't want the breading and they didn't. Most definitely a refined portion so I see they aren't going for a big old slab of comfort food. Instead they are going for comfort-refined. Hot chocolate is that comforting decadence that has a lava cake sort of theme. I mean it is a good thing we walked home afterward because we needed to burn it off. It was a harmonic experience. Atmosphere, staff, food and everything all came together and made each other part even better. I guess even the covers of tunes we knew now make even more sense. They are going for that thing you always knew but hadn't had so good. We got it good. Thanks team Spraga. See you again.

text: For a long time, I turned up my nose at Mellow Mushroom because of the *ridiculous* psychedelic mushroom theme which is all over the outside and inside of the place. Fortunately, tales of their awesome happy hour forced me to overlook the bad paintings. I am here literally every week. My fellow grad students and I usually come here for happy hour before one of our weekly evening events. We almost always share the Mega Vegetarian, which is quite good. I also quite like the capri sandwich on wheat, as well as the capri appetizer. I've gotten a vegan pizza here before with the Daiya cheese (which I'm convinced the manufacturers named such because it's to die for) and it was really tasty. However, I was disappointed that they only had veggie toppings and no seitan or soyrizo. In response to Marcia M, they almost always have at least plain tofu, because it's one of the main components in the Mega Vegetarian pizza that we get every week. One of the things that I really love about Mellow is that all of their pizza components are flavorful--the dough for the pizza is not bland and the tomato sauce is also good but doesn't overwhelm the pizza. And they are usually generous with their toppings. I know they have pizza by the slice at lunch, but I've never been there early enough to try it. One of the main draws here is their crazy amazing happy hour. Half-priced drafts (a solid selection) from 3-8 M-Th and all day Sunday. Wait-service here is a craps shoot. There's one waitress and one waiter whom I adore and are always on the ball. But almost as often, we get someone who will forget to come back and check on whether we need more drinks or if we're ready for the check. That can be really frustrating when you're on a time crunch especially, which we usually are. Also, once every three times we're here, they are changing out one of the kegs and even though they say it'll be just a minute, one of us ends up waiting an extra 15 minutes for our beer. My advice: if your beer is being swapped, save yourself the trouble and order something else. One other thing I just wanted to let people know about coming with a big group. I tried to arrange a big lunch here for 18 people last month, knowing that they had that back room and that you could reserve it. When I actually tried to do so, there was (I believe) a $50 reservation fee and I was told that the food and drink minimum was $250. The thing is, when you're sharing pizzas, it's not going to cost as much, and if you're coming for lunch, people are probably not going to be ordering drinks.. So I asked if there was any way to reserve one of the side sun-room areas or anything and the response I got was a blanket no. Because of this, we ended up at Pie in the Sky which was very accommodating (though sadly their pizza is not as good). To sum up: the food is good, the drink specials are great, the service is hit or miss. Most days, they're good enough for me to chance it.

text: From folklore to Bangalore, even Vishnu, who would have to aggressively flail every arm on his body to get service here, would frown on such epic indifference. Was the food good? Yes. But in the words of a restaurant manager for whom I once worked, "Great service can overcome mediocre food, and bad service can curdle great food." In my last review, I gave four stars to a diner which has notoriously sub-par service that is offset by well above average fare, which kind of negates my manager's maxim. Or does it? Maybe. In the latter case, I think they try, but can't quite nail it. In the former, they could nail it, but don't try. Honestly, I was never really even spoken to at at Flavor of India. Upon entering, I stood in the foyer for a couple minutes before being acknowledged from afar with a shout of "Just a minute, sir." A booth was hurriedly set, and I was waved in from across the restaurant. Upon my triumphant land grab, I beamingly waited for the dulcet tones of a drink order request . . . and waited . . . . . . and waited. Finally, I tired of waiting and sauntered off to the buffet. The vegetarian choices were satisfactory, which one might expect when eating Indian food. I returned to my booth hungry and thirsty, finding a nice glass of ice water awaiting my return. In return I awaited, and awaited, and finally after a couple polite excuse mes, was finally able to assert that I would, in fact, rather enjoy a King Fisher. And I did, in fact, enjoy my King Fisher, and eagerly awaited an offer to partake once again . . . and awaited . . . and awaited. Finally after awaiting away in Prohibitionville, a server broke into my periphery, and with table full and glass empty, wordlessly plopped a check before my visage. "Excuse me," I pleaded, "I'd like another beer, please," as I chucked the check to the other side of the table. Wordlessly, the hand descended to reclaim the swimming pool blue grid with numerical inscriptions, jerking it back into the abyss. I was more fortunate than that poor piece of papyrus, receiving water, barley, hops and yeast in a bottle. I imbibed gratefully as the server offered to take my now long empty plate. I acquiesced, and he suggested that I keep my fork. One of my pet peeves is when a waitron doesn't simply remove any soiled eating utensils perched on plate, and return with fresh. Natch. Put yer dirty tines on the table top, oh so recently swabbed with dirty club soda and smeared with swimming bacteria. Sheesh. Is it that hard and costly to just bring a clean fork? And never once did mortal nor deity inquire as to my satisfaction. Feh. Rotten service spoils good - not great, but good - food. Will I return? Maybe. But I'll bring semaphores and a spotlight if I do.

text: I dined at Scarlett Begonia on a Sunday around noon and was initially very impressed with the location, in the Arlington Plaza, which is very quiet and hidden away from the busy downtown SB area during the summer. We waited around half an hour which wasn't too bad. However at this point I ceased to be impressed by anything else during my dining experience. About 15 minutes after we were seated we were finally greeted by a waitress. She took our drinks and then waited another 15 minutes to ask for our food orders. The daily menu which is all made in house(this was stressed by our waittress) only has about 6-7 different brunch entrees. Three of us ordered the Chilequiles and another ordered the regular breakfast. About 10 minutes later we were told they were out of chilequiles, and could not offer us any sort of substitute, we decided on one of the other 2 breakfast entrees. It seems a little ridiculous that they would run out of one of the three breakfast entrees before 1pm on a Sunday, and then not offer any sort of substitute. I asked for my soft scrambled eggs, to be scrambled hard and the waitress immediately told me no accommodations could be made, even after three of us had to change our orders. By this time we had still not received our drinks. When we finally received our food, three meals came out while the fourth originally ordered dish was never entered. When the fourth meal was finally brought it did not resemble in the slightest another in our party who had the same entree. All in all, after spending almost 2 hours of a Sunday afternoon at Scarlett Begonia I left feeling unfulfilled and only impressed slightly by their Maple Bacon Biscuit. I can say for sure I will not be returning to Scarlett Begonia after their slow, unaccommodating service.

text: As a Reno, NV native, we get great 'que from around the world at the Best in the West Bar-B-Que cookoff every year. While these ribs wouldn't win at our competition, it's only because they are so tender that they can't stick to the bones. The smoke flavor is an excellent smooth flavor, as opposed to the sharp smoke you get in other smokehouses. The texture is excellent as well. My pulled pork sandwich was excellent as well, and was exceptionally moist. We ate at "the Shed" (As seen on Food Network) in Ocean Springs, MS and while it was pretty decent (and their sides were excellent), this place has got it beat hands down. My only complaint would be that the smoked ribeye (haven't seen that before) was a little dry, but the owner was aware of the issue and addressed it for us. He seems to be addressing the issue and is trying to get more consistent on this difficult cut of meat. While on the topic of the owner, the place is family owned and operated, and treats their customers like their business depends on it. As such the staff is impeccably attentive to your needs, and feels more like sitting down at their kitchen table for Sunday dinner than sitting down at a quick service joint. I look forward to returning years later and taking my wife here for some of the best BBQ in the US.

text: Although I'm not Filipino I've been living in Cebu for most of the past year while waiting for my wife's visa to come through, so I am very familiar with how this food is "supposed" to taste. Back home for a visit I remembered this place and stopped in for a taste. I have been very pleasantly surprised with the results. The location is nothing to crow about but the interior is clean and spacious enough. Filipino television and newspapers will welcome you, along with the hospitality of the Filipino management. The food can be as authentic as you want (including diniguan, the famous pigs blood stew) but features plenty of entrees that will appeal to Western palates as well. Some food is prepared ahead and served cafeteria style, while other entrees are made to order and delivered to your table. I had a small fried bangus (milkfish), often described as a Filipino national dish. It was excellent and could have passed for fresh. The most celebrated "national dish" is pork (or chicken) adobo, which was a very tender stewed pork belly in the trademark soy and vinegar broth. It was good enough to spoon up the extra juices with a spoon. The obligatory skewer of BBQ pork completed the basic ensemble. The marinade was tasty and just a little sweet for a very credible effort. For a splurge (and planning to take most of it home as it is my favorite Filipino dish) I ordered spicy sissig, which was made to order. Like sausage, this is a dish you want to try BEFORE doing a lot of research into the recipe ( which includes some of the things that typically end up in sausage in the West!), but if you like pork then sissig will probably appeal to you as well. The version served here is fantastic. Full of complex flavors and delightful spices. My only complaint is that they don't serve beer, which is the traditional accompaniment in the Phillipines. Portions were generous and the food was warm and fresh. Ingredients are very high quality throughout, which is reflected in the pricing across the menu. While certainly fairly priced by American standards (Filipino cuisine is very meat-intensive) I was nevertheless in for a bit of sticker shock after getting used to the pricing in Cebu. This is a lot cheaper than a plane ticket though, and the food is just as good. I haven't read the other reviews yet, not wanting to be biased by those opinions, but I'll admit to being a bit surprised by the aggregate rating, which I think is way too low, particularly given the type of establishment we're talking about. Since I can't give them half-stars I'm going with the full 5. I think this food deceives it.

IF you find parking, IF you get a good seat without waiting too long, IF you go on a day with good beer specials, and IF you get lucky on a good dish, 12 South can be pretty rad. This place seems to be missing the details. The food could stay the same, but they could make some adjustments to give customers a much better experience. Add more staff members. This is a yellow dish, which a lot of people not familiar w/ Indian cuisine may shy away from because of it looks (to be frank) like a yellow mush.w/ vegetables in it, but it is soooo good. It's a mild curry, very little spice at all, but tons of flavor w/ mixed vegetables. One of my favorite things here! 6) Goat - This looked like a braised beef in a brown sauce. It was very good, but most pieces still had chunks of bone attached to them, and you had to cut/eat around them. That's most of what I remember, but it was all very good. I ordered the Strawberry Cheesecake ($3) and they talked me in to adding the Condensed milk ($.50) which I was hesitant about but trusted the experts and did. Fleur De Lis Flavors is a great addition to Nashville and the perfect treat on any hot Nashville night!

text: Mixto is nestled in the Old City section downtown. Not far from South Street or the historical section of Philadelphia. I am not one to go into my actual order of food and drink. I'm too drunk for all that. No, seriously... Mixto has a a flair with placing the pizazz in the simple. Their menu is not extensive, and the dishes are not exquisite. But, what they have is a blend of traditional cuisine with a "DASH" [Shout out to Kim] of contemporary fusion. The price isn't exorbitant. The Spanish Oil paintings with hanging masks and exposed interior columns give it an authentic feel. The drinks and the quiet trance of the music will delight you. text: I REALLY want to like this restaurant. I mean - I've had 3 bad experiences there, and for some reason I will still probably go back again. Maybe I'm destined to suffer until this place finally gets it right. I think the location is great - lots of parking - and convenient if you've been shopping or headed to a movie. Also I like french cooking - so another thing going for them! And honestly - when the food comes out right, it is VERY good. Unfortunately the service is absolutely terrible. The last time I went there I ordered a salad with the dressing on the side. When it came out - it was drenched in dressing. I commented politely that I had asked for the dressing on the side - and the server incredulously asked if I wanted him to take it back. I told him yes - and without a word or apology he walked off with the dish. My friend I was eating with laughed at how rude he was, and decided to wait to eat his food while I waited for mine. Well - he eventually had to start eating so his food wouldn't get cold because it took 25 minutes for my salad to come out! After the salad finally arrived, it was pretty tasty! Disappointingly, we didn't see our server for another half hour - well after our drinks had run up, and a good 15 minutes after we had finished eating and were waiting for the check. Once the check arrived and plates were cleared we waited for our credit card to be taken - but once again the server was nowhere to be found. Ultimately - we just took the bill to the hostess and let her find our server. The time before that I ordered the pan seared duck breast - which was delicious! However, our table of 6 had ordered a few appetizers - one was the daily flat bread. My friend took a piece and he said it was too salty to even eat. A few of us tried the same piece - and it was WAY too salty. So here we were, with a full flat bread, minus half a piece and we asked the server if we could either get another appetizer as a replacement or just take it back. He told us he didn't think he could do that - and told us that he'd have to check with the manager. So our uneaten flat bread stayed on the table until long after our main courses arrived. Almost finished with the meal, the server told us we could have another "appetizer". There wasn't even an apology offered. We declined the replacement. Overall - the food is fantastic - but getting your food prepared correctly and in a timely fashion is an uphill battle. If you've got thick skin and don't mind rude or absent servers - you'll be fine. If the food wasn't so good and I wasn't near the mall so often - I would definitely have given this place 1 star - and have never gone back again.

In the parking lot, I suspected we were in trouble as I could hear the music of a terrible cover band blasting away inside. My assessment of their musical ability did not improve as we entered the place. Furthermore, at a table near the door, I began to notice the unmistakable cackles of middle-aged, suburbanites out for a night on the town. At approximately 7:30pm, these walking examples of indulgence-run-amok were completely hammered and yelling nonsensical comments at the top of their shrieking lungs. Reader, I bet you can guess what table I got to sit next to. That's right, nestled between the ridiculous band and the cackling housewives. Ambiance aside, the food fell into 2 categories: fried and fried. It's not a place for vegetarians; nor is it really a place for people who like good, thoughtful food. The whole menu is a combination of Red Lobster and SYSCO food services. Frenchy's...you're on the water, presumably there are some local fishermen that would sell their catch to you. Oh, but then you'd need to learn how to prepare it. That's hard. Just stick to flash frozen, precooked garbage. Way, way easier. And a better profit margin! The drinks were also very, very weak. We ordered several of the specialty drinks (think well booze, and artificially flavored sugar water, frozen or on the rocks)...all of which disappointed. Oh yeah, they were served in plastic cups. Plastic cups are for toddlers and frat parties. Not for adults or restaurants. Bottom line: Terrible food, horrible ambiance, and drinks you could serve a pregnant lady without fearing fetal alcohol syndrome.

text: Whoever described the ambiance as "divey" was spot on! What a hidden gem off the well (b)eaten path of the surrounding St. Charles area. A few of us came here for a friend's birthday. We initially started off at the bar. They had some good specials and nice beers on tap. The Tchoupitoulas IPA was a perfect way for me to end the day. Imagine my surprise when a small door above the bar opened and a lady popped out bearing po-boys for the dudes at the bar next to us! I thought I had just stumbled into the New Orlean's version of the Keebler elf cookie tree. We took our beers upstairs. I kinda wish they brought the cool vibe of the downstairs bar to the upstairs... since the decor is seriously lacking up there. Ordering is super informal, with the cooks also taking the cash/orders and then cooking it. Our large order came out a bit slowly, but we were having a good time and so didn't mind waiting. Specials were up on the board next to the little food ordering window. Friends that had the highly recommended roast beef po-boys were not disappointed. We all also tried the friend onion rings (not what I'm used to, but delicious nonetheless) and the friend macaroni and cheese (recommended by the cooks). Ok, I'm not normally a fan of friend mac 'n cheese, but it was delicious! Perfectly fried on the outside and warm/gooey on the inside. Plus the dipping sauce was - what else - more cheese. Yay. My red beans and rice was super yummo. I would consider their recipe more of a meat heavy chili-like variety, so I was super full after about 3/4 of the dish. It also came with an unexpected side of nicely toasted and buttered bread (probably from a po-boy loaf of something). Hints: you can walk upstairs to order food without having to go through the bar downstairs. There is a nice dog named Leroy who belongs to the bar area, make sure not to step on him/put your bar stool on his tail!

text: When I stray from my healthy eating in any way, stepping into Whole Foods pretty much makes me want to repent my bad food sins. I'm not much of a fruit eater (I prefer veggies), but the produce here makes me want to fill up my basket full of fruit (and whatever else- but it's the point that I actually want to buy this stuff that I generally don't like to eat). Of course, once I get home, I still end up not wanting what I've bought (fruit-wise) and have to remember that I paid a lot of money for that! Better eat it! I like that I can stop here on my lunch and pick up a hot buffet meal (and a GOOD one), pizza, sushi, soup, clam chowder, salad, sandwiches, etc. It's like a one stop shop for any type of ready-made lunch you could want. And you can grab pretty much any grocery item, too. So while I grab lunch, I can also grab snacks for later- a block of cheese and crackers to snack on, pita and hummus, some nuts. Whatever! The prices are pretty steep, though, of course. And Whole Foods has some effect on you that makes you want things you don't really want otherwise- or NEED (you know, cool organic novelty items). There have been a few times where I've walked up to the cash registers with maybe three things in my hands and a couple cashiers had stuck out their "Next register" sign (with the light still on), and I'd have to stand and wait behind someone with a whole month's worth of groceries while employees stood around chatting at the service desk. Coincidence? It'd be helpful if there was an express lane for people with just a few items or buying a meal. Maybe there is and I never noticed?

text: Had probably been here once before in the mid 90s. But I understood they'd renovated, and now they were offering brunch on Saturday and Sunday. Curiosity got the best of me. It was time to give Rexy's a chance. Ooh look, it's less dungeon-dive and more polite villa. Someone was having a bridal shower in one of the rooms, that's promising. Drink options were exciting to read. The actual product however, merely okay. My expectations were a little high considering the place actually is a bar. We wound up looking at both the brunch and the lunch menus, ultimately choosing sandwiches from the lunch menu in addition to the calimari appetizer that appeared on the brunch menu. There were good efforts to try to get us what we were wanting our sandwiches to be. While there's a chicken parm entree, there's no chicken parm sandwich. So we asked to have the broccoli rabe from my man's chicken cutlet to be put on my pork sandwich (instead of me having to order the broccoli rabe side at an additional $5), and they did give him a condiment cup of sauce for his chicken cutlet sandwich. I recognize calimari can be a hit or miss item, so they weren't off to a good start. We picked at a few limp flavorless pieces, then abandoned. Our sandwiches came with a salad. Mesculin with parmesan shavings and a thick balsamic. Serviceable, but we wouldn't have minded there being something beyond just some damn lettuce. Picked at it, abandoned. Just unnecessary. Then came the sandwiches. Not disastrous, but it didn't save the experience. Though my roast pork was nicely seasoned, the sandwich was so soggy it melted the mediocre roll and the pieces were cut very irregularly - sometimes a sliver, sometimes a fatty chunk. I wasn't taking home my leftovers, just ate the broccoli rabe from the sandwich with a fork. We were asked by two different people if everything was good. We answered that it was okay, haltingly, only to have repeated to us, "Good? Good!" And then the check came, and it was surprising. Drink prices hadn't been listed so we didn't know what a hit we were taking on those, but each and every one of the food items we'd ordered came up on the bill as a dollar or two more each than they had on the menu. Shadiness. So we wound up prolonging our stay just to deal with this, which turned also into a conversation regarding our honest answers as to whether or not we enjoyed our meal. We were already feeling uncomfortable about complaining, this isn't who we are. Believe me, I wanted to enjoy this. I always want more brunch options, but this one was a sorrowful experience.

text: This place is such a slice of heaven, that I don't even know why I am talking about it! You park there, go to the north/west end and follow a path under the overpass, behind a home or two and down an access road to the beach. The beach backs up to some cliffs and you can walk quite a way up and down the coast during low tide, but the beach is quite small/intimate at high tide. If you are coming South on the 101 you would use Exit 90, go right and then a quick left and you will see the parking lot. Follow the directions above. Quiet. Serene. Beautiful gliding pelicans. The sparkle of the sun on the blue ocean currents. Rocky cliff formations. Sigh. Forget I told you about this place, please....

Paled in comparison to better octopus dishes in the city (Estia, Positano Coast, Dmitri's). The red pepper sauce was nice, though. The biggest disappointment was the lamb shank. I have never experienced a more bland lamb shank. It looked great, but it just didn't deliver--at all. Dessert was nice. We opted for the doughnuts. A little on the spicy side. But for two people they gave us three doughnuts. A big pet peeve of mine--if there are two people, just throw another doughnut on the plate so we can each have two. The stuffed basket of nan was a nice touch and the chutneys were good--especially that green one. Overall, the meal was severely lacking in flavor. Where was that spicy Indian punch throughout the meal? Service was a bit intrusive and we could never really hear any of the servers very well. We were also surprised that the manager never stopped by our table to say hello or check on our meal. We were there for a good hour and a half and the restaurant wasn't filled to capacity, plus it's still relatively new so you would have expected at least a quick visit by the manager. so tasting menu for two, three cocktails and a $190 bill after tip we expected to leave happy and impressed, but we left thinking of a big "meh." Nights like this make me wonder why I eat anywhere other than Zahav.

text: Okay, I don't get it. I'm of the school of thought that says, "Don't knock it 'til you've tried it twice." So after an underwhelming experience at the Sausage Deli a few months ago, I stopped in for another try. Last time I had gotten the Bismarck sub, only to suddenly appreciate how important it is for pastrami, sauerkraut, and co. to be served on bread with some firmness to it. The Sausage Deli's microwaved white bread sub just didn't cut it, and made the entire sandwich feel floppy and sad (the flavor, I should add, was nothing to write home about either, though it wasn't bad). Today I decided to change directions and opt for the barbecue special, which is offered only on Tuesdays and Fridays. I figured that floppy, microwaved bread wouldn't be half as bad if it were filled with delicious barbecued beef, and I might have been right if the beef had been delicious. But alas, it was just so-so, and when combined with the lameness of the bread, I was left wondering why I insisted on coming back at all. So call me a hater, I guess, but I just don't see how this place could possibly deserve 4.5 stars. There's just nothing particularly good about it as far as I can tell, and the bread totally ruins all of their hot sandwiches (which I ascertain to be the point of this place). Maybe there's something I'm missing?

text: Great food and fantastic atmosphere. Decor/Ambiance: Gorgeous red wood tables all cut from one huge tree are unique with great texture and shapes (mine was a little awkwardly high because of the variance in the thickness of the wood but not much of an issue) The walls are speckled with awesome art and it is trendy but relaxed. Staff: They're new and many are pretty green BUT I've gone a couple times and each time they are getting more of the hang of it and in a few weeks I'm sure they'll be in top shape. I may have had to ask for a knife or a spoon after it gets swept up by a busser without being replaced but I can live with that. The Drink: I'm not much of a drinker but the selection of beers is really top notch and the server said they offer a craft beer of the month for $3 always which is damn good. I opted for the house filtered and sparled water which is great with some lime and done as well as in Daniel Boloud's restaurants (I'm living full time in NYC) The Food: The menu is HUGE. I tried a bunch of stuff but below are my FAVORITES: Fig, bacon, balsamic pizza - Of course it's good, look at the ingredients. Great play of flavors The stuffed meatball - monstrous, perfectly seasoned, falling appart and wonderful. Short Ribs - These were rich, hearty and great. (not for a dieter unless you have at least a partner in crime to share them with) Chicken Parmigian - This is my sweetspot in an italian restaurant. The key to my heart and they unlocked the pandora's box of chicken parm. juicy, pounded thin chicken breasts lightly breaded and sauced to perfection. I opted for a thin speghetti for my pasta and it was just as I wanted. As you can see from the above items I didn't have much room for desert but those waffles look awesome.. something to go back for the next time I'm trekking through the So. Jersey area. Overall. Do it. come. Eat. Enjoy. If I lived closer I'd go and hang out at the outdoor bar all the time. Beautiful ambiance, full bar, tv's and a fire pit.. I hope they bring out a Smore plate for people curled around the fire.

text: Okay, I had high hopes that some REAL smoking and brisket, port and chicken had arrived in Collegeville. I don't think so. I saw the set up in the back and I suspect the meat is simply roasted in a smoker. No smoke ring or deep flavor was noted. We ordered brisket, chicken, pulled pork and sides. Disappointed big time. No smokey aroma, no smoke rings could be found. The chicken was barely cooked; oozing blood from the leg/thigh joint. Very light rub without flavor. The chicken skin looked weird...white without any smoking appearance. Boring flavor. BBQ is only available if you ask for it, and there's only one type. Huh? The brisket tasted like it had been slow roasted on a grill...NOT truly smoked. Not much flavor. Pulled chicken was pathetic. Chicken pieces tossed with BBQ seasonings. Big deal. The mac and cheese arrived in one gelatinous mass. umm....no. Green beans? Slimy and cooked without pork or onion flavorings. No cornbread accompanied any of our orders, although the menu stated they would. Beans were nothing special. Service was poor. It reflected poor training. It wasn't that the servers weren't trying or lacking effort...things were chaotic and food took way, way too long to arrive.. It was lunch time and only 5 other tables were filled. The manager needs to immediately go to ZACHARYs BBQ in Norristown to sample their BBQ and learn what a smoke ring looks like. What a dry rub looks like on smoked chicken. Chicken with the pink smoke ring is a beautiful thing! Then there's the 5 sauces that house made and incredible.

Given rent is extremely expensive having a 9 mo lease (which we were told we could never get) is a HUGE savings if you aren't going to need the apt during the summer. They grudgingly let us take advantage of the $300 deal - only because of their screw up in not getting us a lease out even though everything was supposedly settled in May. The office staff seems nice enough when you come in or call ... but they are (were, maybe - supposedly there was a well deserved change over) totally ineffective. Dozens of all calls and follow up all stating we were good - everything in order (we even mentioned the requested roommates everytime we called to ensure there were no problems) ... yet we were in the 11 hr. getting a lease with a random roommate after being assured everything was fine. Roommate assignments and instructions were promised in mid July and came maybe a week or two before move in. According to the new mgt, the problems were attributable to the former management ... Given the trouble with getting the lease and still trying to abide by our contract, I went online to try to pay the rent on time only to learn that I'd be charged a $25 'convenience fee' for an online payment - that's a joke! They could have had the money immediately, but waited for me to send it via snail mail ... what business sense does that make? Adding insult to injury even on move in day, my daughter had to re-sign ANOTHER lease since there was a typo on the one she had already signed. Go over all the details on this place with a fine tooth comb. As expressed by others, the reasons we selected this place: security and location. text: The Library II used to be a family favorite...so we returned recently when back in the area to celebrate our son's birthday. What happened to this previously top-rated restaurant?? When our plates arrived, she hastily barked out our orders, incorrectly naming my dish as "extremely well-done rib eye" - which should've been our second clue about the quality of the Library II. I told her that I ordered Prime Rib, well done but juicy. What I was served was indescribable. I've had Prime Rib at the Library on many occasions and it was always delicious and juicy, even though I request it to be well-done. On this visit the meat was blackened and difficult to cut. The inside was completely dried out and leathery, no meat juices at all. They obviously had over-cooked it badly. Out of our four meals, only one was cooked correctly. My son's medium filet was rare (purple), another's chicken kiev was pink - we asked the server to take it back to the kitchen to check it - she said it was cooked and just "juicy." My husband is a fan of the london broil and that was cooked to perfection. Our server didn't return to ask the rest of us how our food was cooked. text: I had watched a 3-day marathon of HGTV Design Star before checking into the hotel, so I was incredibly critical of the decor and workmanship of the room. text: I live in Wayne and drive past Matador everyday, so when I had been hearing that they were opening this restaurant, the suspense was really building up. When it finally opened, my aunt and I went for dinner right away. Like me, she is a big fan of tapas, so we seek them out wherever we are. Unfortunately, our experience at Matador fell flat. It started when we walked into a half-full restaurant with a hostess telling us there would be a wait unless we had reservations. Then she sat us at a table downstairs (practically sitting inside the hostess booth) which was smashed against the wall. We are petite girls, and even we found it to be a tight squeeze. Then the waiter- a super friendly guy- who didn't quite know how to properly pronounce the Spanish names on the menu was nice. His mispronunciation was more funny than actually bothersome. Then came the food: we had a few unmemorable tapas, each of which was saltier than the last. The salt overpowered the food so much that we couldn't tell one thing from the next. One thing I will praise is the tableside guacamole. It certainly isn't the best guac, but I'm glad they decided to do this (since it's a kind of rarity in the suburbs).

Maybe just for me. The baklava was funky, nothing like Hellas. Not even close. If you are looking for good baklava, look elsewhere. The atmosphere is nice and the service is excellent. text: I had been wanting to try Yang's for some time. Because I don't frequently get to Mid-City, it had been sitting in my to try list for a while. I quickly sped to Bienville and ordered a sandwich. I decided on a roast beef poor boy since those are my favorite, and a great judge of a restaurant's quality. While Yang's version was a traditional New Orleans style poor boy (proper bread, etc.), it wouldn't rate in my top ten. I enjoyed it, but it seemed to be missing something that I can't totally explain. I realize that isn't helpful, but I just can't put my finger on what it needed. As a side I tried their cheese fries with gravy. They came with nacho type cheese, which I do not like. I would not order this again. So if the poor boy was just OK, why four stars? Any restaurant that was open prior to, or immediately after a hurricane deserves an extra star. Since the other reviews of Yang's are so positive, I will be back. text: It may not look like much, but Alla Spina's Pig Pot Pie is an otherworldly delight. We liked the bibb lettuce and pig trotter wraps, too. I wish there were more than two. We felt that the poutine with guinea hen bolognese and mozzarella curd was a bit too salty. The decor feels a lot like Osteria with its seating arrangements facing a bar and open air kitchen. A big pig hangs over the bar tempting you to try any of Alla Spina's porcine delights. It wasn't until I later that I learned that what I had enjoyed was an Italian Gastropub experience, so if beer is your drink of choice, this is the place. Even my prosecco, vodka, and lemon sorbet cocktails were fashioned to look like champagne glasses of beer with froth on top. The restaurant felt a little like Amis and a little like Osteria. text: I wanted to love this restaurant. I really, really did. I was excited about coming here because of all the positive things that were being said. Unfortunately, my experience did not live up to the hype. I'll first say that it's a beautiful space with an intimate ambiance. When you walk in, you're greeted by a gorgeous bar and a chalkboard with wine specials. The bartenders are quick to greet to ensure you're not waiting for a table for longer than necessary. My group was five people and we started with a cheese and charcuterie platter. While the server was funny and friendly, she wasn't able to tell us where the prosciutto was from and given that d'Lish advertises itself as a restaurant that supports eating locally, this was surprising. When my friend asked a second time where the proscuitto was from (after he hadn't received an answer the first time and after we were served the dish), the server answered, "What does it matter? You'll eat it anyway." What kind of response is that?! The three cheeses and two meats were tasty but this was overshadowed by the poor response to the very valid question posed about where the meat came from. Our mains ranged from salmon to rabbit to gnocchi to a vegetarian gratan. The best of these dishes was the gnocchi - it was cooked well and had great balance of flavour. I wish I'd ordered that instead of the rabbit, which had great sides and a nice beet glaze but was cooked far too long and had the texture of packed sawdust. Overall, the portion sizes were too small for the $25+ being charged for each dish. The desserts were the best course overall. I had a chai creme brulee and it was served with a pastry crust, which was a welcome departure from every other creme brulee I've eaten. My friend's panna cotta was "the best" she's ever eaten - the texture and flavours were great. The 2 out of 5 rating may seem harsh. But I can't overlook the fact that the rabbit, the whole point of my main course, was cooked to the point of being bone dry. No amount of glaze (and there was a lot) or tasty sides hid this fact. Aside from this, d'Lish very obviously advertises the fact that it's a localvore restaurant. If you billet yourself as such, make sure your staff are trained to speak about the food and don't offer seafood. If you aren't prepared to be scrutinized, don't make claims. I contrast this with one of the best meals I had this year at Lee in Toronto. The server knew absolutely every detail about the menu: where every ingredient was from, which dishes were celiac-friendly, how each dish was prepared. She never once had to check with the kitchen to answer these questions and the restaurant didn't make claims about what they were or weren't trying to do (e.g. supporting local producers because they didn't, exclusively, and offered seafood items). Finally, the menu is confusing: is it a tapas menu or a more traditional one? Why both? The best restaurants choose one theme and execute it to the absolute best of their ability. I feel that ambitions are high here but the execution doesn't live up. At least not yet. Many of the producers providing ingredients for the restaurant are people I know or who are friends of the people in my group. One of the main reasons we went to the restaurant is to support these producers. After this experience, we will support them elsewhere.

text: Blah-blah-I'm-wasted-blah. I speak for every local when I say that Bourbon Street is a must-try-at-least-once place, but after that, forget it. It's pretty much drunks, beads, cheesy tees, over-priced drinks, pushy shot girls and very, VERY dirty shoes. Your classless tourist trap that somehow people stumble away from smiling, only to have the worst hangover you've ever had the next morning. Definitely try it... once. Maybe twice, a third? No thank you... Guide: Don't wear flip-flops. Don't let anyone tell you what you "Got yo' shoes" - it's the stupidest joke to get money out of you. Shot girl shooters are $3, they will try to rip you off 4 out of 5 times. Don't ride the bull at Bourbon Cowboy panty-less Don't pee on the in public - that's what they'll arrest you for. DO just enjoy yourself, sing karaoke at Cat's Meow, try a hurricane at Pat O's, dance at Razzoo or the Beach or the Cowboy or any other joint on the street. DO tip the Lucky Dog workers when you get a dog. It hits the spot after dancing a ton, trust me. But TIP - the vendors do not own the stand. [EDIT] Places to check out: - Maison Bourbon Jazz Club at the end of the 600 block - great jazz music if you are willing to cram into the small space they offer and pay for a 1 drink minimum per set - Bourbon Cowboy - recently moved to 500 or 600 block (5 or 6 blocks away from Canal). They play gung-ho country jams and have a bull. - The Dungeon - just off Bourbon St at 738 Toulouse (5 blocks from Canal). A dark, divy nightclub that plays metal - Pat O'Brien's - Sit in the courtyard and drink a famous Hurricane drink or hit up the piano bar for a musical experience even the locals love. - For a dance scene - Razzoo and The Beach on Bourbon are the best spots to get hot and sweaty. - Karaoke - definitely check out Cat's Meow if you have a dare to execute or bring out the inner Carrie Underwood in you. text: This is one of the better places to eat in Metairie and one of the better French restaurants in the area. I've been to dinner here several times and lunch a few times. The lunch is a pretty good deal while dinner can get more pricey. They use great quality ingredients and have some fantastic wine with a much more scanty selection of beers. They have the BEST hamburger in all of Metairie and one of the best in the entire NOLA metro area (you can add foie gras too for $10 extra if you're feeling extra decadent). All of the sandwiches, including the burger, come with perfect fries fried in duck fat! This is a great spot for a pleasant lunch, a romantic dinner, or a night out with a group of friends. The only mediocre meal I ever had here is when I came with a big group that had a set menu and they ran out of beer. They do some great French food here and you always get to start your meal with some of their great bread and butter so come prepared to enjoy yourself! Hint 1: The parking is right off Metairie Road so it can be a bit challenging to pull out and most folks angle park to make it easier to get out and see the oncoming traffic. Hint 2: If you like wine then the wine reps usually show up on Tuesdays at lunch time and you can hear some interesting discussion about wine that is being sampled.
